lpp.card_network.table_type_reason: Very small static lookup table (11 rows) containing only descriptive attributes for card schemes; no measures or transactional data.
lpp.card_network.grain: One row per card payment network or scheme.

lpp.card_rebate_earning.description: This table records the rebate amounts earned by each corporate entity under their respective card rebate programs for each reporting period, broken down by spend category and rebate tier achieved. It captures eligible spend, the rebate earned, the currency, and the tier level attained (BASE, TIER1, TIER2) per quarter-end period. Key identifiers include uuid (PK), program_ref, company_ref, period_date, and spend_category.
lpp.card_rebate_earning.table_type_reason: Contains additive numeric measures (eligible_spend, rebate_earned) recorded at a periodic grain per program, company, and spend category — characteristic of a periodic fact table, not a dimension.
lpp.card_rebate_earning.grain: One row per card rebate program, company, reporting period (quarter-end date), and spend category combination.

lpp.card_rebate_program.description: This table defines the terms and configuration of each corporate card rebate program, including the issuing bank, enrolled company, program type (purchasing card, virtual card, commercial card), spend tier threshold, and the rebate rate in basis points awarded at target. It also tracks the effective date range for each program agreement. One row represents a single card rebate program agreement between a bank and a corporate entity.
lpp.card_rebate_program.table_type_reason: Small configuration/master-data table (4 rows) describing rebate program terms; serves as a lookup for the card_rebate_earning fact table.
lpp.card_rebate_program.grain: One row per card rebate program agreement between a corporate entity and an issuing bank.

lpp.card_settlement_batch.description: This table records each card settlement batch submitted by the merchant for processing, capturing the full financial waterfall from gross sales through to net settlement including refunds, chargebacks, interchange fees, network assessments, and processor margins. It tracks key timestamps for batch close, processor settlement, and bank deposit, enabling reconciliation of card revenues with bank account credits. Key identifiers include uuid (PK), acquirer_ref, network_code, and bank_account_ref.
lpp.card_settlement_batch.grain: One row per card settlement batch submitted by the merchant to an acquirer on a given card network.

lpp.card_settlement_line.description: Represents individual line items within a card payment settlement batch, capturing the full fee breakdown for each settled card transaction. Each record links a specific card authorization to its settlement batch and details the gross transaction amount, interchange, network assessment, processor margin, and other fees, yielding the net amount payable to the merchant. Key identifiers are uuid (primary key), batch_ref (settlement batch), and authorization_ref (original card authorization).
lpp.card_settlement_line.table_type_reason: Contains multiple additive financial measures (gross_amount, interchange_amount, net_amount, etc.) per settled card transaction event, making it a transactional fact table rather than a reference table.
lpp.card_settlement_line.grain: One row per individual card transaction line item within a settlement batch, linked to a specific card authorization.

lpp.cash_balance.description: Records the daily cash balance for each treasury bank account under various viewing configurations (transaction date vs. value date, and inclusion flags for actual, intraday, confirmed, and estimated flows). Each row represents a specific account's balance on a given date for a particular combination of date basis and transaction inclusion flags, enabling multi-dimensional cash position reporting. Key identifiers are account_ref, balance_date, date_basis, and the four boolean inclusion flags that together form the composite primary key.
lpp.cash_balance.grain: One row per bank account, balance date, date basis, and combination of inclusion flags (actual, intraday, confirmed, estimated).

lpp.cash_flow.description: Captures individual cash flow transactions and forecasts across all treasury bank accounts, recording both confirmed (actual posted) and forecast (estimated future) movements of funds. Each record represents a single cash flow event with its originating account, flow type, counterparty, transaction and value dates, amounts in both flow and account currency, and the payment rail used. Key identifiers are uuid (primary key), account_ref, flow_code_ref, counterparty_ref, and reference (source system traceability UUID).
lpp.cash_flow.table_type_reason: Contains multiple additive monetary measures (flow_amount, signed_amount, account_amount) per cash flow event with rich dimensional attributes; it is a transactional/event fact table rather than a dimension table.
lpp.cash_flow.grain: One row per individual cash flow transaction or forecast entry, identified by a unique UUID.

lpp.cash_flow_code.description: A reference lookup table defining the standardised classification codes used to categorise cash flow transactions across the treasury system. Each record defines a unique cash flow code with its human-readable description, directional sign (IN/OUT), and cash flow statement category (OPERATIONS, INVESTING, FINANCING). Key identifiers are uuid (primary key) and code (the alphanumeric classification code used as a foreign key in lpp.cash_flow).
lpp.cash_flow_code.grain: One row per distinct cash flow classification code.

lpp.chargeback.description: Tracks card payment chargeback disputes from initiation through resolution, covering details of the disputed transaction, the acquiring bank, card network, reason codes, monetary amounts, and the merchant's representment efforts. Each record represents a single chargeback case tied to an original card authorization, with lifecycle status (INITIATED, REPRESENTED, WON, LOST) and root-cause classification (TRUE_FRAUD, FRIENDLY_FRAUD, MERCHANT_ERROR). Key identifiers are uuid (primary key) and authorization_ref (the original disputed transaction).
lpp.chargeback.table_type_reason: Represents discrete chargeback dispute events with measurable monetary amounts and lifecycle state, characteristic of a fact table rather than a reference table.
lpp.chargeback.grain: One row per individual chargeback dispute case, linked to a specific card authorization.

lpp.company.description: This table represents legal entity master data for all companies within the corporate group. Each row describes a single legal entity with its registered name, country of incorporation, and a set of regulatory and financial identifiers. Key identifiers include uuid (primary key), code (e.g. GR_AU), LEI, SEPA creditor identifier, and tax IDs.
lpp.company.table_type_reason: Classic entity master / dimension table describing legal entities with descriptive attributes and identifiers; no measures or facts present.
lpp.company.grain: One row per legal entity (company) within the corporate group.

lpp.company_financial_metric.description: This table stores periodic financial performance and balance sheet metrics for each legal entity within the group, covering P&L items (revenue, EBITDA, net income), cash flow measures (free cash flow, capex), debt and capital structure figures, and derived ratios (leverage, WACC, interest coverage). Each row captures a snapshot of a company's financials for a specific reporting period and period type (quarterly or full-year). Key identifiers are company_ref, period_date, and period_type.
lpp.company_financial_metric.table_type_reason: Contains many numeric financial measures (revenue, EBITDA, debt, ratios) keyed by company and period — classic periodic snapshot fact table, not a reference table.
lpp.company_financial_metric.grain: One row per legal entity, reporting period date, and period type (e.g. quarterly or full-year).

lpp.company_group.description: This table defines the corporate group structures used to organise legal entities into regional or consolidation segments (e.g. GROUP_EMEA, GROUP_APAC, GROUP_GLOBAL). Each row represents a named group with a machine-readable code and a human-readable description of its scope. Key identifiers are uuid (primary key) and code.
lpp.company_group.table_type_reason: Small lookup table (6 rows) defining a fixed set of group codes and labels — classic reference/lookup data.
lpp.company_group.grain: One row per company group (regional or consolidation segment).

lpp.company_group_member.description: This bridge table maps individual legal entities to one or more company groups, enabling many-to-many relationships between companies and groups (e.g. a single entity can belong to GROUP_GLOBAL and GROUP_EMEA simultaneously). Each row represents a single membership assignment linking a company code to a group code. Key identifiers are the composite primary key of company_group_code and company_code.
lpp.company_group_member.table_type_reason: Resolves a many-to-many relationship between company groups and companies with a composite PK and no measures — a bridge/association table.
lpp.company_group_member.grain: One row per company-to-company-group membership assignment.

lpp.counterparty_exposure.description: This table tracks the organisation's financial exposure to each counterparty bank as of a daily reporting snapshot, broken down by exposure type: deposits, investments, and derivative mark-to-market values. Each row captures the aggregated exposure to one bank on one date, expressed in a reporting currency with a percentage-of-portfolio concentration metric. Key identifiers are as_of_date and counterparty_bank_ref.
lpp.counterparty_exposure.table_type_reason: Periodic snapshot of numeric exposure measures (deposits, investments, derivative MTM, total exposure, % of total) keyed by date and counterparty — a snapshot fact table, not a reference table.
lpp.counterparty_exposure.grain: One row per counterparty bank per reporting snapshot date.

lpp.credit_facility.description: This table represents the master register of credit facilities available to the organization's legal entities, including revolving credit lines, term loans, overdrafts, commercial paper programs, and intercompany arrangements. Each row describes a single facility agreement between a borrowing entity and a lender bank, capturing its financial terms, tenor, and current status. Key identifiers include the system UUID, the human-readable business code (e.g. CF_RCF_USD_2B), company_ref, and lender_bank_ref.
lpp.credit_facility.table_type_reason: This is a slowly-changing master register of credit facility agreements, not a transactional fact table; it serves as a dimensional reference for drawdown and utilisation facts.
lpp.credit_facility.grain: One row per credit facility agreement between a borrowing legal entity and a lender bank.

lpp.credit_rating.description: This table stores the credit ratings assigned to the organization's legal entities by external rating agencies (Moody's, S&P, and Fitch), including the rating grade, outlook, and the action taken at each review date. Each row represents a single rating event for a specific entity-agency combination at a point in time, with an is_current flag to identify the latest active rating. Key identifiers include the system UUID, company_ref, agency, and as_of_date.
lpp.credit_rating.grain: One row per credit rating record for a legal entity issued by a specific rating agency on a given date.

lpp.cross_border_payment_leg.description: This table captures individual legs of cross-border payment transfers, recording the full economics of each leg including send and receive amounts, currencies, the FX rate and spread applied, lifting and correspondent fees, and the payment rail used. Each row represents one leg of a cross-border transfer routed through a specific geographic corridor between an origination and destination country. Key identifiers include the leg UUID, parent transfer_uuid, and payment_transaction_uuid.
lpp.cross_border_payment_leg.grain: One row per individual leg of a cross-border payment transfer, linking a parent transfer to its specific origination country, destination country, currency pair, and payment method.

lpp.currency.description: This table is the system reference list of currencies supported by the platform, containing the ISO 4217 code, full name, decimal precision, settlement float in business days, and display flags for each currency. Each row defines a single currency and its operational attributes used to drive payment processing, FX calculations, and UI presentation. Key identifiers include the system UUID and ISO currency code.
lpp.currency.table_type_reason: This is a static lookup/reference table for currency codes and attributes used across the system.
lpp.currency.grain: One row per ISO 4217 currency supported by the platform.

lpp.data_permission.description: This table defines the data access control rules that govern which permission profiles are authorised to access specific companies or bank accounts within the system. Each row maps a permission profile code to a single entity (company or bank account), enabling role-based data visibility and entitlement management. Key identifiers include the record UUID, profile_code, entity_type, and entity_code.
lpp.data_permission.table_type_reason: This is a security/access-control entitlement mapping table that acts as a reference for governing data visibility rather than storing business transactions or dimensions.
lpp.data_permission.grain: One row per combination of permission profile and entity (company or bank account) to which that profile is granted access.

lpp.data_permission_profile.description: This table defines the named data permission profiles used to control access to data across the platform. Each record represents a distinct permission profile encoding a geographic scope (Global, Americas, EMEA, APAC) and an access level (full read/write, read-only) or a functional role (e.g. AP operations). Key identifiers are the system UUID and the machine-readable profile code such as PROF_GLOBAL_FULL or PROF_EMEA_RW.
lpp.data_permission_profile.table_type_reason: Small, stable lookup table (7 rows) enumerating named permission profiles; purely referential with no measures or event timestamps.
lpp.data_permission_profile.grain: One row per named data permission profile.

lpp.derivative_mtm.description: This table records the daily mark-to-market (MTM) fair value of derivative instruments, specifically FX forward contracts, as of each valuation date. Each record captures the fair value of a specific derivative instrument on a specific date, linked to the internal legal entity that holds the position and the external bank counterparty. Key identifiers are instrument_ref (e.g. FXF-0000107), valuation_date, company_ref, and counterparty_bank_ref.
lpp.derivative_mtm.table_type_reason: Contains time-series quantitative measures (mtm_amount) at the instrument-date grain with 36,569 rows sorted by valuation_date; clearly a fact table, not a reference table.
lpp.derivative_mtm.grain: One row per derivative instrument per valuation date.

lpp.equity_action.description: This table records corporate equity events executed by group holding entities, including share buybacks, regular dividends, and special dividends. Each record represents a single equity action event with its action and settlement dates, share count, price per share, total payout amount, and the named corporate program under which it was conducted. Key identifiers are the UUID and the program_name, with company_ref always being GR_HOLDINGS.
lpp.equity_action.table_type_reason: Contains transactional measures (shares, total_amount, price_per_share) tied to specific dated events (action_date, settle_date); this is a fact table capturing corporate equity events, not a reference table.
lpp.equity_action.grain: One row per corporate equity action event (buyback, dividend, or special dividend) per action date.

lpp.fee_rate_card.description: This table stores the bilaterally negotiated fee rates agreed between the company and its banking partners for specific banking services. Each record defines the rate charged by a particular bank for a given service code, including the billing unit (per transaction, per month), the applicable currency, and the effective date range during which the rate is valid. Key identifiers are the UUID, bank_ref, service_code, and company_ref, with effective_from and effective_to defining the rate validity window.
lpp.fee_rate_card.table_type_reason: Confirmed reference/rate table — stores negotiated pricing schedules rather than transactional events or measures; appropriate override from inferred reference type.
lpp.fee_rate_card.grain: One row per bank, service code, company, and effective date range combination.

lpp.forecast_cash_flow.description: This table stores projected cash flows by legal entity, account, and forecast period, grouped by business category (e.g. AR collections, AP disbursements, debt service, CAPEX) and organized into discrete forecast snapshot runs identified by a snapshot_id. Each record captures the expected monetary inflow or outflow for a given entity and account in a specific forecast month, along with an analyst confidence level and a seasonality adjustment factor. Key identifiers are UUID, snapshot_id, company_ref, account_ref, forecast_date, and flow_category.
lpp.forecast_cash_flow.table_type_reason: Contains quantitative forecast measures (forecast_amount, seasonality_factor) across multiple entities, accounts, and time periods with 2,660 rows sorted by forecast_date; clearly a fact table rather than a reference table.
lpp.forecast_cash_flow.grain: One row per forecast snapshot, company, account, forecast date, flow category, and flow subcategory.

lpp.forecast_snapshot.description: Represents a versioned forecast run or snapshot, capturing the metadata for each time a forecasting model was executed. Each record defines the forecast's publication date, the horizon window it covers, the time granularity of its data points, and the model version used. Key identifier is snapshot_id, encoded as FC_YYYYMMDD_[cadence] (e.g. FC_20230801_M for a monthly run).
lpp.forecast_snapshot.table_type_reason: This is a reference/dimension table of forecast run metadata — each row describes a distinct forecast snapshot entity, not a measurable event or fact.
lpp.forecast_snapshot.grain: One row per distinct forecast snapshot run, identified by a unique snapshot_id combining forecast date and cadence.

lpp.forecast_vs_actual.description: Tracks the comparison between planned and realised cash flow amounts for each legal entity, reporting period, and cash flow category, linked to a specific forecast snapshot. Each record contains the forecasted amount, actual amount, and both absolute and percentage variances, enabling forecast accuracy analysis. Key identifiers are company_ref, period_date, flow_category, and snapshot_id.
lpp.forecast_vs_actual.table_type_reason: Contains multiple additive numeric measures (forecast_amount, actual_amount, variance_amount, variance_pct) at a well-defined business grain — this is clearly a fact table, not a reference table.
lpp.forecast_vs_actual.grain: One row per combination of legal entity, month-end period, and cash flow category for a given forecast snapshot.

lpp.fraud_detection_event.description: Records individual fraud evaluation events raised by the fraud detection system against payment transfers or files. Each event captures the fraud risk score, the automated decision outcome (ALLOW, REVIEW, or BLOCK), the structured reason codes driving that decision, and the timestamp when the event was raised. The primary key is a UUID, with optional links to a transfer_uuid or file_uuid.
lpp.fraud_detection_event.table_type_reason: Each row represents a discrete scored fraud evaluation event occurring at a specific timestamp — this is an event/fact table, not a dimension.
lpp.fraud_detection_event.grain: One row per fraud detection event raised by the fraud screening system, identified by a unique UUID.

lpp.fraud_loss.description: Captures confirmed fraud loss incidents at the transaction level, recording the monetary loss and any amounts subsequently recovered. Each record links to a fraud detection event and a payment authorisation reference, and classifies the loss by type (friendly fraud vs. true fraud), attack vector, sales channel, and authentication method used. Key identifiers are the record UUID, detection_event_uuid, and authorization_ref.
lpp.fraud_loss.table_type_reason: Contains additive monetary measures (loss_amount, recovered_amount) representing realised fraud loss events — clearly a fact table rather than a reference table.
lpp.fraud_loss.grain: One row per confirmed fraud loss incident, identified by a unique UUID and linked to a specific payment authorisation.

lpp.fx_exposure_forecast.description: Stores forward-looking foreign exchange exposure forecasts for each legal entity, broken down by currency pair, tenor bucket, and origination source. Each record quantifies the gross exposure amount and indicates whether the position is long or short, as of a specific snapshot date and for a given forecast period. The primary key is a UUID, with company_ref, forecast_period, exposure_currency, and tenor_bucket serving as the natural business key.
lpp.fx_exposure_forecast.table_type_reason: Contains an additive numeric measure (gross_exposure_amount) at a well-defined multi-dimensional grain — this is a fact table representing forecasted FX positions, not a dimension.
lpp.fx_exposure_forecast.grain: One row per legal entity, forecast period, tenor bucket, exposure currency, direction, and origination source combination as captured on a given snapshot date.

lpp.fx_forward.description: This table represents individual FX forward contracts executed by group legal entities with external bank counterparties. Each record captures the full economics of a single deal, including the contracted buy/sell currencies and amounts, the agreed forward rate versus spot rate at trade date, and the contract's current lifecycle status (OPEN, SETTLED, CANCELLED). Key identifiers are uuid (system PK) and deal_id (business reference, e.g. FXF-0001164), with company_ref and counterparty_bank_ref linking to internal entity and bank dimensions.
lpp.fx_forward.table_type_reason: Each row records a discrete transactional FX forward deal event with measurable amounts, rates, and a lifecycle status — characteristic of a fact table, not a reference table.
lpp.fx_forward.grain: One row per FX forward contract deal executed by a group legal entity with a counterparty bank.

lpp.fx_rate.description: This table stores daily foreign exchange rates between currency pairs, sourced from providers such as Bloomberg, the ECB, or internal systems. Each row captures the exchange rate for a specific base/quote currency pair on a given date, qualified by rate type (e.g. SPOT) and data source. Key identifiers form a composite PK of rate_date, base_currency, quote_currency, and rate_type, supporting multi-source and multi-type rate lookups.
lpp.fx_rate.table_type_reason: This is a slowly-changing reference/lookup table of market rates used for currency conversion across the platform, not a transactional dimension describing a business entity.
lpp.fx_rate.grain: One row per currency pair (base and quote currency), rate date, and rate type combination.

lpp.gen_company_region.description: This table is a small reference dimension mapping each group legal entity (company code) to its geographic business region and functional currency. With only 24 rows it represents the full universe of group entities, enabling regional roll-ups and currency-aware reporting. Key identifier is company_code (e.g. GR_APAC_PTE, GR_BR), with region (EMEA, APAC, LATAM, AMER, MENA) and functional_ccy as descriptive attributes.
lpp.gen_company_region.table_type_reason: This is a small, static lookup/mapping table (24 rows) linking company codes to regions and currencies — a reference table rather than a true analytical dimension.
lpp.gen_company_region.grain: One row per group legal entity (company code).

lpp.gl_account.description: This table is a reference dimension cataloguing all general ledger accounts across the group's ERP systems (SAP, NetSuite, Oracle). Each record defines a GL account with its structured code, human-readable description, balance sheet classification (ASSET, LIABILITY, REVENUE, EXPENSE, EQUITY), owning legal entity, functional currency, and an optional link to a specific bank account. Key identifiers are uuid (system PK) and code (business key, e.g. '1110-GR_AU_OPERATING_1').
lpp.gl_account.table_type_reason: With 451 rows this is a static chart-of-accounts catalogue used as a lookup/dimension across ERP systems — best classified as a reference table.
lpp.gl_account.grain: One row per general ledger account as defined within a specific ERP chart of accounts for a legal entity.

lpp.gl_balance.description: This table stores month-end closing balances for each general ledger account across the group's ERP systems. Each record captures the monetary balance of a specific GL account at the end of a calendar month, denominated in the account's currency, along with the source ERP system. Key identifiers form a composite PK of gl_account_ref, balance_date, and balance_type, enabling point-in-time balance lookups per account per period.
lpp.gl_balance.table_type_reason: Each row is a periodic (month-end) financial measurement (balance amount) against a GL account — a classic periodic snapshot fact, not a dimension.
lpp.gl_balance.grain: One row per GL account, month-end balance date, and balance type (closing).

lpp.gl_reconciliation.description: This table records the monthly bank-to-general-ledger reconciliation performed for each bank account across the group. Each record captures the bank balance and GL balance as of a month-end date, together with the variance amount, currency, and reconciliation status (MATCHED or INVESTIGATING). Key identifiers are the UUID primary key, bank_account_ref (e.g. GR_DE_OPERATING_1), and gl_account_ref (e.g. 1110-GR_DE_OPERATING_1).
lpp.gl_reconciliation.table_type_reason: Each row is a measurable reconciliation event with balance and variance amounts at a point in time, making it a fact table rather than a reference table.
lpp.gl_reconciliation.grain: One row per bank account and month-end reconciliation date.

lpp.hedge_dedesignation.description: This table records instances where a formal hedge accounting relationship was de-designated, capturing the date, amount, company, currency, and business reason for each de-designation event. It serves as an audit log of hedge relationship terminations driven by events such as corporate restructuring or early termination of the underlying instrument. Key identifiers are the UUID primary key and hedge_ref (e.g. HR-0001216).
lpp.hedge_dedesignation.table_type_reason: Each row represents a discrete business event (de-designation) with a date and monetary amount, making it a fact table rather than a reference table.
lpp.hedge_dedesignation.grain: One row per hedge relationship de-designation event.

lpp.hedge_relationship.description: This table represents each formal hedge accounting relationship established by a group entity, capturing its classification (fair value, cash flow, or net investment), the hedged exposure type and currency, the associated FX forward instrument, notional amount, and current lifecycle status. It tracks the full lifecycle from designation through to active, terminated, or de-designated states. Key identifiers are the UUID primary key, the business code (e.g. HR-0000518), and instrument_ref (e.g. FXF-0000518).
lpp.hedge_relationship.table_type_reason: This table is a slowly-changing descriptive register of hedge relationships with status and attributes, making it a dimension rather than a reference table.

lpp.intercompany_transaction.description: This table records individual intercompany financial transactions between group entities, including the originating (source) and receiving (target) companies and their respective bank accounts, the transaction amount and currency, and the business purpose (e.g. funding, loan, dividend, royalty). Each record is linked to corresponding cash flow records on both the source and target sides. Key identifiers are the UUID primary key and the human-readable reference (e.g. IC-0008991).
lpp.intercompany_transaction.table_type_reason: Each row represents a discrete financial transaction event with an amount, date, and directional flow between entities, making it a fact table rather than a reference table.

lpp.interest_accrual.description: This table records daily interest accrual entries generated by borrowings, investment positions, and credit facility fees across all group entities. Each record captures the accrued amount in the original currency, the direction (income or expense), and links back to the source financial instrument via source_type and source_uuid. Key identifiers are the UUID primary key, source_uuid (the originating instrument), and company_ref.
lpp.interest_accrual.table_type_reason: Each row is a time-stamped financial accrual with a measurable monetary amount, making it a fact table rather than a reference table.
lpp.interest_accrual.grain: One row per interest accrual entry per source instrument per accrual date.

lpp.investment_instrument.description: This table is a reference catalogue of all financial instruments available for investment by the treasury function, covering types such as money market funds, time deposits, certificates of deposit, treasuries, commercial paper, repos, and bonds. Each row represents a single investable instrument with its defining static attributes including issuer, currency denomination, coupon rate, issue/maturity dates, and credit rating. Key identifiers are the surrogate key `uuid` and the human-readable business code `code` (e.g. INV_MMF_0014).
lpp.investment_instrument.grain: One row per investment instrument defined in the treasury instrument catalogue.

lpp.investment_position.description: This table records daily point-in-time snapshots of the treasury's holdings across all investment instruments, capturing the face value, market value, book value, accrued interest, yield to maturity, and remaining duration of each position. Each row represents the holding of one investment instrument in one investment bank account as of a specific reporting date. Key identifiers are `uuid` (surrogate), `instrument_ref` (links to investment_instrument), `bank_account_ref`, and `as_of_date`.
lpp.investment_position.table_type_reason: Contains multiple additive financial measures (face_amount, market_value, book_value, accrued_interest) snapshotted daily — clearly a periodic snapshot fact table, consistent with the inferred type.
lpp.investment_position.grain: One row per investment instrument held in a specific bank account as of a given reporting date.

lpp.investment_transaction.description: This table records individual investment transactions executed by the treasury, including purchases of new instruments, coupon/interest receipts, and principal returns at maturity, across instruments such as repos, certificates of deposit, time deposits, and bonds. Each row represents a single investment transaction event with its trade date, settlement date, amount, price, and yield locked in at trade. Key identifiers are `uuid` (surrogate), `instrument_ref`, `bank_account_ref`, `trade_date`, and `transaction_type`.
lpp.investment_transaction.table_type_reason: Represents discrete financial events (purchases, coupons, maturities) with measurable amounts — a transactional fact table, not a reference table as inferred.
lpp.investment_transaction.grain: One row per investment transaction (purchase, coupon, or maturity event) executed against an investment instrument.

lpp.kg_relationship.description: This table stores directed relationships between pairs of entities in the corporate knowledge graph, capturing the type of relationship (e.g. owns, employs, is_part_of), the source and target entity types and codes, and metadata about how and when the relationship was captured. Each row represents a single directed relationship between two identified entities, along with its confidence score, status, and semi-structured properties. Key identifiers are `uuid`, the combination of `from_entity_code` / `from_entity_type` and `to_entity_code` / `to_entity_type`, and `relationship_type`.
lpp.kg_relationship.table_type_reason: This table links two entity nodes via a typed relationship — structurally a bridge/association table between knowledge graph entities, not a standard dimension.
lpp.kg_relationship.grain: One row per directed relationship between two entities in the knowledge graph.

lpp.letter_of_credit.description: This table tracks all letters of credit (LCs) issued on behalf of group companies by their banking counterparties, covering both standby and commercial LC types used for purposes such as trade finance, utility deposits, self-insurance, and tax deferment. Each row represents a single letter of credit instrument with its issuing bank, applicant company, beneficiary, face amount, drawn amount, fees, currency, and lifecycle status. Key identifiers are `uuid` (surrogate), `lc_number` (e.g. LC-2024-00021), and `credit_facility_ref`.
lpp.letter_of_credit.grain: One row per letter of credit issued to a beneficiary on behalf of a group company.

lpp.liquidity_policy.description: This table stores the set of treasury liquidity rules and constraints that govern how much cash or liquidity a company or group must maintain at any given time. Each record defines a single policy rule — such as a minimum cash buffer, a maximum counterparty concentration percentage, or a maximum instrument tenor — scoped to a specific legal entity or regional group. Key identifiers are uuid (primary key), company_ref, and company_group_ref, with thresholds expressed either as absolute monetary amounts (threshold_amount/threshold_currency) or percentages (threshold_pct).
lpp.liquidity_policy.table_type_reason: With only 10 rows and date-effective policy rules scoped to entities/groups, this is a slowly-changing reference/configuration table rather than a transactional dimension.
lpp.liquidity_policy.grain: One row per liquidity policy rule per company or company group, covering a specific policy type and effective date range.

lpp.macro_indicator.description: This table captures time-series readings of key macroeconomic indicators used to inform liquidity planning and forecasting decisions. Each record holds the observed value of a specific indicator (e.g. Federal Funds Rate, SOFR 3M, US CPI, Brent crude oil price) for a given region and date, along with its unit of measurement and source institution. Key identifiers form a composite primary key of indicator_code, region, and as_of_date.
lpp.macro_indicator.table_type_reason: This is a time-series reference/lookup table of external macroeconomic data points used as inputs to forecasting models, not a transactional fact table.
lpp.macro_indicator.grain: One row per macroeconomic indicator code per region per observation date.

lpp.mapping_entry.description: This table holds individual key-value translation entries belonging to various cross-reference lookup tables used across the treasury platform. Each record maps a source code or identifier to its corresponding target value within a named mapping table — for example, translating a payment rail code (WIRE, ACH) to its AFP service code, or a cash flow type to a GL account class. Key identifiers are the composite primary key of mapping_table_code and source_value.
lpp.mapping_entry.table_type_reason: This is a generic cross-reference/translation lookup table, not a transactional dimension.
lpp.mapping_entry.grain: One row per source value within a named mapping table.

lpp.mapping_table.description: This table is the parent registry of all named mapping/translation tables used across the treasury platform, with only 4 rows representing distinct mapping types. Each record defines a mapping table by its machine-readable code and a human-readable description of the source-to-target translation it performs (e.g., 'Payment rail → AFP service code'). The primary key is uuid, with a unique code acting as the natural key referenced by lpp.mapping_entry.
lpp.mapping_table.table_type_reason: This is a metadata registry table cataloguing available mapping/translation tables, not a transactional dimension.
lpp.mapping_table.grain: One row per distinct mapping table definition.

lpp.membership_fee.description: This table records individual membership fee transactions issued to members across the company's subsidiaries and sales channels. Each record captures a single fee charged to a specific member for a given membership tier (Gold, Executive, Business), including the fee amount, collection channel, payment method, membership validity period, and collection outcome (collected, failed, chargeback, refunded). Key identifiers are uuid (primary key) and member_id, with company_ref linking to the issuing subsidiary.
lpp.membership_fee.table_type_reason: With 30,000 rows, monetary amounts (fee_amount, fraud_loss), statuses, and event dates, this is a transactional fact table recording fee collection events, not a dimension.
lpp.membership_fee.grain: One row per membership fee transaction per member.

lpp.payment_exception.description: Records individual payment exceptions detected during payment processing, capturing the root cause, detection and resolution timestamps, and the cost and effort required to remediate each issue. Each row represents a single exception event tied to a specific payment file or transfer, classified by type such as BANK_VALIDATION, FILE_FORMAT, OFAC_HOLD, or DUPLICATE. Key identifiers are uuid (exception record), file_uuid (source payment file), and transfer_uuid (the triggering transfer).
lpp.payment_exception.table_type_reason: Contains event-level records with measures (resolution_time_minutes, repair_touch_count, repair_cost_amount) and timestamps, making it a fact table rather than reference.
lpp.payment_exception.grain: One row per payment exception event detected in the payment processing pipeline.

lpp.payment_file.description: Represents ISO pain.001 XML payment instruction files submitted from internal legal entities to the banking network, tracking transmission status, routing completion, and aggregate value. Each row corresponds to a single payment file batch originated from a specific company and bank account, identified by file_uuid. Key attributes include company_ref, account_ref, status (SENT/RECEIVED/NACK), total transaction count, and total amount in the file's currency.
lpp.payment_file.table_type_reason: Tracks individual file submission events with status lifecycle, aggregate amounts, and counts — behaves as a transaction/event fact rather than a static dimension.
lpp.payment_file.grain: One row per payment instruction file submitted to the payment hub.

lpp.payment_hub_throughput.description: Stores daily aggregated operational metrics for the payment hub, broken down by payment rail (ACH, WIRE, RTP, SEPA_CT) and country, capturing volumes, values, success/rejection/repair counts, and straight-through processing (STP) rates. Each row represents a summary of payment activity for a specific date and payment rail combination processed through the originating system (e.g. KYRIBA_PAYMENT_HUB). Key identifiers are uuid, metric_date, and payment_rail.
lpp.payment_hub_throughput.table_type_reason: Contains daily aggregated measures (volume_count, value_amount, success_count, rejection_count, stp_rate_pct) across dimensions — this is a periodic snapshot fact table, not a reference table.
lpp.payment_hub_throughput.grain: One row per payment rail per metric date reported by the payment hub.

lpp.payment_transaction.description: Records individual payment transactions included within payment files, capturing the full lifecycle from initiation through execution or rejection across multiple payment rails. Each row represents a single payment instruction identified by its ISO 20022 end-to-end reference, with details on the issuing entity and account, beneficiary counterparty and account, amount, currency, and the payment rail used. Key identifiers are uuid, file_uuid, and end_to_end_id.
lpp.payment_transaction.table_type_reason: Captures individual payment events with amounts, statuses, and timestamps — a transaction-level fact table rather than a dimension.
lpp.payment_transaction.grain: One row per individual payment transaction submitted through the payment hub.

lpp.peer_company.description: A reference list of external peer companies used for competitive benchmarking, storing each company's ticker symbol, full name, industry sector, peer group classification, and country of headquarters. Each row represents one peer company identified by its ticker-style code. Key identifiers are code and ticker (e.g. WMT, AMZN, HD).
lpp.peer_company.grain: One row per peer company included in the benchmarking universe.

lpp.peer_company_metric.description: This table stores financial and operational benchmark metrics for a defined set of peer/competitor companies (e.g., Walmart, Amazon, Home Depot, Kroger) across reporting periods. It captures key performance indicators such as revenue, EBITDA, free cash flow, leverage ratios, return on capital, and payments-related metrics like interchange rates and fraud losses. One row represents a single peer company's reported metrics for a specific period end date and period type (quarterly or full-year).
lpp.peer_company_metric.table_type_reason: Contains multiple additive numeric measures (revenue, EBITDA, FCF, ratios) recorded per peer company per period — classic periodic snapshot fact table, not a reference/dimension.
lpp.peer_company_metric.grain: One row per peer company (peer_code), reporting period end date (period_date), and period type (period_type).

lpp.pension_plan.description: This table is a master reference list of the company's defined pension plans across different countries and legal entities. Each record describes a single pension plan, including its country of operation, plan type (defined benefit or hybrid), sponsoring entity, and whether it is open to new participants. Key identifiers are the system UUID, the structured plan code (e.g., PP_US_DB), and the company reference code.
lpp.pension_plan.table_type_reason: This is a slowly-changing descriptive master record of pension plans with no measures — a dimension table, not a reference lookup.

lpp.pension_valuation.description: This table records periodic actuarial valuations of the company's pension plans, capturing funded status, projected benefit obligations, plan asset fair values, and key actuarial assumptions such as discount rate and expected return on assets. It also includes projected employer contributions for the next three years and the OCI impact of actuarial deviations. Each record represents the valuation of a specific pension plan as of a particular valuation date.
lpp.pension_valuation.table_type_reason: Contains multiple numeric measures (PBO, plan assets, funded status, contributions, OCI) snapshotted at a point in time per plan — a periodic snapshot fact table, not a reference.
lpp.pension_valuation.grain: One row per pension plan (plan_ref) and valuation date (as_of_date).

lpp.pos_transaction.description: This table records individual point-of-sale transactions processed across the company's retail channels, including in-warehouse, e-commerce, kiosk, mobile app, and membership renewals. Each record captures the transaction amount, currency, payment method, sales channel, store location, associated member (if any), and the register or terminal used. Key identifiers are the transaction UUID, member ID, and location/register codes.
lpp.pos_transaction.table_type_reason: Each row is a discrete transactional event with a monetary amount and multiple dimensional attributes — a transactional fact table, not a dimension.

lpp.sme_feedback_session.description: This table tracks structured feedback sessions conducted with subject matter experts (SMEs), recording who participated as both the SME and interviewer, the session start and end times, the topic discussed, and a URI pointing to the session transcript. It is used to capture and organize qualitative knowledge-gathering interactions, likely in support of data governance or knowledge graph enrichment workflows. The key identifier is the session UUID.
lpp.sme_feedback_session.table_type_reason: Describes discrete sessions as business entities with descriptive attributes and no additive measures — better classified as a dimension than a generic dimension; override from inferred dimension is consistent so keeping it.
lpp.sme_feedback_session.grain: One row per SME feedback session (uuid).

lpp.sme_transcript_chunk.description: Represents a segmented chunk of a Subject Matter Expert (SME) session transcript, broken into ordered pieces for indexing and semantic search. Each row captures a single text segment from a specific session, along with its position in the transcript and its vector embedding metadata. Key identifiers are uuid (chunk ID), session_uuid (parent session), and opensearch_doc_id (search index reference).
lpp.sme_transcript_chunk.grain: One row per segmented text chunk extracted from an SME session transcript.

lpp.stress_run_result.description: Records the outcome of a liquidity stress test run for a specific scenario, company, and month-end date. Each row captures the minimum projected cash balance, the breach threshold, the projected breach date (if any), and the severity level for a given scenario-entity-period combination. Key identifiers are uuid (result ID), scenario_ref, company_ref, and run_date.
lpp.stress_run_result.table_type_reason: Contains quantitative outcome measures (min_projected_cash, threshold_amount, breach_severity) produced by stress test executions — characteristic of a fact table, not a dimension.
lpp.stress_run_result.grain: One row per stress scenario run per company entity per month-end run date.

lpp.stress_scenario.description: A reference catalogue of liquidity stress test scenarios used to define the shock assumptions applied during stress runs. Each row defines a named scenario with its type, a human-readable description, and a structured JSON parameters object encoding quantitative shock inputs. Key identifiers are uuid and code (e.g. STR_AR_DROP_20, STR_RATE_PLUS_200).
lpp.stress_scenario.table_type_reason: Small static lookup table (6 rows) defining scenario codes and parameters — correctly classified as reference.
lpp.stress_scenario.grain: One row per defined stress test scenario.

lpp.sweep_execution.description: Records each individual cash sweep execution event triggered by a sweep instruction, capturing the funds moved from an operating source account to a concentration target account on a given date. Each row includes the swept amount, pre- and post-sweep balances, residual amount, execution status, and links to the resulting debit and credit cash flow records. Key identifiers are uuid, instruction_ref, source_account_ref, target_account_ref, and execution_date.
lpp.sweep_execution.table_type_reason: Contains transactional event measures (swept_amount, pre/post-sweep balances) per execution date — this is a fact table, not a reference table.
lpp.sweep_execution.grain: One row per sweep instruction execution on a given date.

lpp.sweep_instruction.description: Defines the standing rules that govern automated cash sweeps between source operating accounts and target concentration accounts across the group's entities. Each row specifies the sweep mechanism type (ZBA, TARGET, NOTIONAL_POOL, THRESHOLD), direction, target balance, schedule, priority, and validity period for a single source-to-target account pairing. Key identifiers are uuid and code (e.g. SW_GR_CA_OPERATING_1).
lpp.sweep_instruction.table_type_reason: Small slowly-changing configuration table (38 rows) describing sweep rules — correctly classified as dimension.
lpp.sweep_instruction.grain: One row per standing sweep instruction rule between a source and target account.

lpp.third_party.description: Represents external organisations or counterparties (vendors, partners, customers) that interact with the company in a financial capacity. Each row corresponds to a single third-party entity, classified as either a creditor, debtor, or both, along with attributes such as name, tax identifiers, transaction limits, and portfolio references. Key identifiers are uuid (primary key) and code (business code such as TP_CUST_0001).
lpp.third_party.table_type_reason: This is a master data / dimension table describing third-party entities, not a simple code reference list — it has rich attributes including tax info, limits, and creditor/debtor flags.
lpp.third_party.grain: One row per third-party entity (organisation or individual counterparty) registered in the system.

lpp.third_party_bank_account.description: Stores bank account details belonging to third-party entities such as vendors, counterparties, or external organisations. Each row represents a single bank account associated with a specific third party, capturing the account identifier, branch, currency, and whether it is the default account for payment purposes. Key identifiers are uuid (primary key) and third_party_code (foreign key to the third-party entity).
lpp.third_party_bank_account.grain: One row per bank account belonging to a third-party entity.

lpp.third_party_category.description: A reference lookup table defining the classification categories used to group or segment third-party entities. Each row represents a distinct category with a short alphanumeric code and a human-readable description. Key identifiers are uuid (primary key) and code (business category code).
lpp.third_party_category.table_type_reason: This is a small code/lookup table defining category types, making it a reference table rather than a full dimension.
lpp.third_party_category.grain: One row per third-party category definition.

lpp.third_party_category_assignment.description: A bridge (association) table that maps third-party entities to their assigned business categories, supporting a many-to-many relationship between third parties and categories. Each row represents a single assignment of one category to one third-party entity. Key identifiers are the composite primary key of third_party_code and category_code.
lpp.third_party_category_assignment.grain: One row per assignment of a category to a third-party entity.

lpp.transfer.description: Records individual payment transfers initiated via ISO 20022 pain.001 payment files across multiple payment rails (SEPA CT, WIRE, RTP, ACH). Each row represents a single transfer instruction with its processing status, acknowledgement outcome, remittance references, amount, currency, and value date. Key identifiers are uuid (primary key), transaction_number (human-readable reference), and reference (source document such as an accounts payable invoice).
lpp.transfer.table_type_reason: This table records transactional payment events with amounts, statuses, and dates — it is a fact table, not a dimension, despite the inferred type.
lpp.transfer.grain: One row per individual payment transfer instruction submitted to the payment network.

lpp.tribal_knowledge_entity_link.description: This table represents the many-to-many relationship between tribal knowledge fact records and the business entities associated with them (e.g., persons, organizations, products). Each row captures a specific entity linked to a fact, along with the role that entity plays in the context of that fact (e.g., author, subject, owner). Key identifiers are fact_uuid, entity_type, entity_code, and role, which together form the composite primary key.
lpp.tribal_knowledge_entity_link.table_type_reason: This is a bridge/association table resolving a many-to-many relationship between tribal knowledge facts and business entities, with an additional role attribute.
lpp.tribal_knowledge_entity_link.grain: One row per unique combination of tribal knowledge fact, entity type, entity code, and role.

lpp.tribal_knowledge_fact.description: This table stores individual tribal knowledge facts — pieces of institutional or organisational knowledge captured from users, categorised by type, and enriched with validity dates, confidence ratings, and lifecycle status. Each row represents a single discrete knowledge fact with a free-text title and narrative, a trigger condition describing when it applies, and metadata about how and when it was captured and embedded into a vector search index. Key identifiers include the uuid primary key, source_session, and opensearch_doc_id.
lpp.tribal_knowledge_fact.grain: One row per distinct tribal knowledge fact record.

lpp.user_group.description: This table is a reference list of functional user groups within the platform, representing business departments or operational teams such as Treasury, Accounts Payable, Accounts Receivable, Financial Control, Internal Audit, and Platform Administration. Each row defines a single user group with a short alphanumeric code and a human-readable description. Key identifiers are uuid (primary key) and code (e.g., UG_TREASURY, UG_AP).
lpp.user_group.table_type_reason: Small, low-cardinality lookup table (6 rows) defining static platform user groups; clearly a reference/lookup entity.

lpp.user_group_member.description: This table captures the membership of individual users within functional user groups, linking user codes (representing specific roles such as FX_TRADER or CASH_MANAGER_AMER) to their assigned group codes (such as UG_TREASURY or UG_AP). Each row represents a single user-to-group assignment, and the composite primary key of user_group_code and user_code enforces uniqueness. It serves as the bridge between the user_group and individual user identity tables.
lpp.user_group_member.table_type_reason: This is a bridge/association table resolving the many-to-many relationship between users and user groups.
lpp.user_group_member.grain: One row per unique combination of user group and user.

lpp.user_profile_assignment.description: This table records the access profile assignments for each platform user, defining which permission scope and level each user has been granted (e.g., full global access via PROF_GLOBAL_FULL, or regional read-write access via PROF_EMEA_RW). Each row represents a single assignment of an access profile to a user identified by their functional role code. The composite primary key of user_code and profile_code allows a user to hold multiple profiles.
lpp.user_profile_assignment.table_type_reason: This is a bridge/association table resolving the many-to-many relationship between users and access profiles.
lpp.user_profile_assignment.grain: One row per unique combination of user and assigned access profile.

lpp.v_sme_transcript_chunk_indexable.description: This view represents individual text segments (chunks) extracted from Subject Matter Expert (SME) conversation session transcripts, prepared for vector embedding and semantic search indexing. Each row corresponds to a single ordered chunk of transcript text from a specific SME session, identified by a unique chunk UUID and linked to its parent session via session UUID. Key identifiers include chunk_uuid, session_uuid, and chunk_index (the ordinal position within the session).
lpp.v_sme_transcript_chunk_indexable.grain: One row per individual transcript chunk segment within an SME conversation session.

lpp.v_tribal_fact_indexable.description: This view represents curated 'tribal knowledge' facts — discrete pieces of institutional or expert knowledge captured from within the organisation — prepared for vector embedding and semantic search indexing. Each row corresponds to a single tribal fact record with a lifecycle status, validity date range, confidence rating, and linked business entities. Key identifiers include fact_uuid, with categorisation via fact_type and associated linked_entities.
lpp.v_tribal_fact_indexable.grain: One row per tribal knowledge fact record.

lpp.wcf_document.description: This table represents individual working capital finance (WCF) documents — typically supplier invoices or financing instruments — that form the basis of supply chain finance or early payment programmes between buyers and suppliers. Each row corresponds to a single WCF document linking a specific supplier and buyer legal entity, with an associated amount, currency, issue and due dates, and lifecycle status. Key identifiers include the uuid (primary key), document_number (e.g. WCF-0000641), and supplier_ref.
lpp.wcf_document.table_type_reason: This table records individual financial documents (invoices/financing instruments) with monetary amounts, dates, and statuses — behaving as a fact table rather than a dimension.
lpp.wcf_document.grain: One row per working capital finance document.

lpp.webhook_event.description: This table captures inbound webhook event notifications received from an external or internal payment platform, recording business events such as document approvals, routing status changes, batch status changes, and execution completions. Each row represents a single webhook event tied to a specific business entity (e.g. a PAYMENT_FILE), with a full structured payload and receipt/processing timestamps. Key identifiers include uuid (primary key) and entity_code (the UUID of the affected business entity).
lpp.webhook_event.table_type_reason: This table records discrete system/business events as they occur over time, with timestamps and payloads — making it a fact (event log) table rather than a dimension.
lpp.webhook_event.grain: One row per webhook event received by the system.

lpp.working_capital_metric.description: This table stores periodic working capital KPI metrics calculated at the company-entity level, capturing key measures such as Days Sales Outstanding (DSO), Days Payable Outstanding (DPO), Days Inventory Outstanding (DIO), Cash Conversion Cycle (CCC), accounts receivable and payable balances, and trailing twelve-month revenue and COGS. Each row represents the working capital metrics for a specific legal entity for a given reporting period (month-end or quarter-end date). Key identifiers are the composite primary key of company_ref and period_date.
lpp.working_capital_metric.table_type_reason: This table stores quantitative periodic measures (DSO, DPO, DIO, CCC, balances) keyed by entity and time period, which is characteristic of a fact table, not a reference table.
lpp.working_capital_metric.grain: One row per company entity per reporting period date.

0.description: This community centres on the organisation's knowledge graph infrastructure, combining institutional knowledge capture (tribal facts and SME feedback sessions) with their preparation for vector embedding and semantic search indexing. It also connects acquirer contract data, suggesting that knowledge graph enrichment workflows are used to contextualise and govern commercial payment processing agreements. Analytical questions focus on the provenance, confidence, and coverage of captured organisational knowledge and its linkage to treasury business entities.
query_patterns: Which tribal knowledge facts are linked to a specific acquirer contract, and what is their confidence rating and validity period?
Which SME feedback sessions have generated transcript chunks that have been indexed for semantic search, and what topics did they cover?
What institutional knowledge facts are currently active and ready for vector indexing, and which business entities are they associated with?

1.description: This community connects card rebate programme earnings with working capital KPI metrics at the legal entity level, enabling analysis of how card spend rebates interact with broader working capital health indicators such as DSO, DPO, and Cash Conversion Cycle. Each entity's rebate tier attainment (BASE, TIER1, TIER2) and eligible spend can be evaluated alongside its accounts payable and receivable balances and trailing revenue. This cluster supports questions about optimising payment method choices and their downstream impact on working capital efficiency.
query_patterns: For each legal entity, how does the rebate tier achieved in a given quarter correlate with its Cash Conversion Cycle (CCC) for the same period?
Which companies earned the highest card rebates relative to their eligible spend, and how do their DPO metrics compare?
How has a company's working capital position (AR/AP balances) changed over quarters alongside shifts in its card rebate spend category mix?

2.description: This community covers the liquidity stress testing framework, pairing the catalogue of defined stress scenarios with the results produced when those scenarios are run against specific company entities. Each scenario encodes quantitative shock assumptions (e.g. AR drop, rate shifts) and the results capture projected minimum cash balances, breach thresholds, breach dates, and severity levels. Together these tables support monitoring of liquidity resilience and regulatory or internal stress testing reporting.
query_patterns: Which legal entities breached their liquidity threshold under the STR_AR_DROP_20 scenario in the most recent stress run, and what was the projected breach date?
How do minimum projected cash balances compare across all active stress scenarios for a given company at the latest run date?
Which stress scenarios produced the highest severity outcomes across all entities, and what shock parameters are defined for those scenarios?

3.description: This community represents the platform's identity, access control, and governance layer, covering user accounts, functional group memberships, permission profiles, and data entitlements at the company and bank account level. It also incorporates third-party counterparty data, AI reasoning engine audit trails, and inbound webhook events, reflecting the cross-cutting nature of user-driven interactions with treasury business objects. This cluster can answer questions about who has access to what data, how permissions are structured, and what actions users and automated systems have performed.
query_patterns: Which users belong to the UG_TREASURY group and what data permission profiles have they been assigned?
What audit trail events were triggered by a specific user role (e.g. CASH_MANAGER_AMER) in the last 30 days, and which entity types were affected?
Which permission profiles grant access to a specific set of companies or bank accounts, and how many users currently hold each profile?

4.description: This community represents the organisation's banking master data and fee management framework, encompassing the full hierarchy of banks, branches, and accounts alongside negotiated fee rate cards, billed service fees, and bank account groupings. It also incorporates third-party counterparty and account data, payment acquirer references, and macroeconomic indicator time series used to contextualise liquidity and forecasting decisions. This cluster supports questions about bank relationship cost analysis, fee variance monitoring, account structure management, and the macro environment underpinning banking decisions.
query_patterns: For each bank account, what is the variance between the fees actually charged and the expected fees based on the negotiated rate card for the latest billing period?
Which bank branches serve accounts in a specific currency or region, and what are their payment cut-off times?
How have key macroeconomic indicators (e.g. SOFR 3M, Fed Funds Rate) moved over the past 12 months, and which bank accounts or fee rate cards are tied to floating-rate services in those regions?

6.description: This community focuses on tracking actual capital deployment by legal entity, reporting period, and allocation bucket such as CAPEX, M&A activity, dividends, debt paydown, and share buybacks. Each record captures both the realised deployment amount and the framework target percentage, enabling variance analysis between planned and actual capital allocation. This cluster supports capital efficiency and governance reporting at the entity and group level.
query_patterns: How does the actual capital deployed into CAPEX compare to the framework target percentage for each legal entity in the most recent quarter?
Which legal entities have over- or under-allocated capital relative to their targets across M&A and debt paydown buckets?
What is the trend in actual capital allocation by deployment bucket across all entities over the past four quarters?

7.description: This community covers the organisation's working capital finance operations, spanning accounts payable and receivable invoices, letters of credit, and supply chain finance documents. Together these tables track the full trade finance and invoice lifecycle — from vendor invoices and customer receivables through to structured instruments like LCs and WCF programmes — across group legal entities. This cluster supports end-to-end working capital visibility, trade finance exposure monitoring, and early payment programme analysis.
query_patterns: What is the total open accounts payable balance by vendor and legal entity, and which invoices are overdue or in dispute?
Which letters of credit are approaching expiry, and what is the outstanding drawn versus face amount by issuing bank and company?
How much of the outstanding AR invoice balance is eligible for or currently enrolled in working capital finance (WCF) programmes, broken down by supplier and buyer entity?

8.description: This community focuses on individual borrowing drawdowns made by group entities against their credit facilities, capturing the full lifecycle of each draw including amounts, interest rates, drawdown and repayment dates, and current status. It provides a granular view of debt utilisation across facility types such as term loans, revolving credit facilities, intercompany lines, and overdrafts. This cluster can answer questions about active debt positions, interest cost exposure, and repayment schedules at the entity and facility level.
query_patterns: What is the total outstanding borrowing balance by legal entity and facility type as of today?
Which borrowing drawdowns are due for repayment in the next 90 days, and what are the associated interest rates and currencies?
How much of each revolving credit facility has been drawn down versus the available facility limit, broken down by company?

9.description: This community covers the end-to-end card acquiring lifecycle, from individual authorization attempts and BIN/network lookups through to settlement batching, chargeback dispute management, and acquirer SLA compliance monitoring. It contains transactional fact tables (card_authorization, card_settlement_batch, card_settlement_line, chargeback), reference dimensions (card_bin_range, card_network), and performance metrics (acquirer_sla_metric), supplemented by fraud evaluation events and broader payment rail throughput data. Together these tables support analytical questions around authorization approval rates, fee waterfall reconciliation, chargeback win/loss trends, acquirer performance against SLA thresholds, and fraud-driven card losses.
query_patterns: What is the authorization approval rate by card network and BIN range for each acquirer over the past 30 days, and how does it compare against each acquirer's contracted SLA target?
For chargebacks raised in the last quarter, what proportion were won vs. lost by reason code and acquirer, and what was the total monetary exposure by card network?
What is the net settlement amount payable to the merchant after interchange, network assessments, and processor margins, broken down by acquirer and settlement batch date?

11.description: This community represents the core cash and liquidity management domain, consolidating daily bank statement balances, treasury cash positions, individual cash flow transactions, automated sweep executions, intercompany funding movements, and interest accruals into a unified view of the group's liquidity. It also includes ACH return events, GL closing balances for ERP reconciliation, and reference lookups for budget codes, cash flow classifications, and code mappings. These tables collectively enable treasury teams to monitor intraday and end-of-day cash positions, track intercompany funding activity, reconcile bank balances to the general ledger, and analyse the cost of cash concentration structures.
query_patterns: What is the daily closing cash position for each bank account across all entities this month, and how does it reconcile against the bank statement balance reported in the BAI feed?
Which automated sweep instructions executed last week resulted in a residual balance above the target threshold, and what were the pre- and post-sweep balances for the affected accounts?
What is the total interest accrual expense by legal entity and source instrument for the current quarter, and how does it compare to the prior quarter?

12.description: This community covers the FX risk management and hedge accounting domain, spanning FX exposure forecasting, FX forward contract execution, daily mark-to-market valuation, formal hedge relationship designation and de-designation, and supporting corporate entity and financial metric dimensions. It brings together instrument-level deal data (fx_forward, derivative_mtm), portfolio-level exposure forecasts (fx_exposure_forecast), hedge accounting records (hedge_relationship, hedge_dedesignation), and entity master data (company, company_group, gen_company_region) to provide a complete picture of the group's currency risk profile. These tables support analytical questions around hedge coverage ratios, MTM fair value movements, hedge accounting compliance, and cross-border payment FX costs.
query_patterns: What is the current hedge coverage ratio by currency pair and legal entity, comparing open FX forward notional amounts against the latest FX exposure forecast for each tenor bucket?
Which hedge relationships were de-designated in the past six months, what was the reason, and what is the cumulative MTM fair value impact of those de-designations by company and currency?
What is the total FX spread and lifting fee cost incurred on cross-border payment legs by currency corridor and payment rail over the last quarter?

13.description: This community centres on treasury investment portfolio management and its integration with banking infrastructure and ERP reconciliation. It combines daily investment position snapshots and transaction history (investment_position, investment_transaction) with counterparty bank exposure concentration metrics, GL account definitions and month-end balances (gl_account, gl_reconciliation), credit ratings for entity and counterparty risk assessment, and bank account signatory governance records. Together these tables enable analysis of portfolio yield and duration, counterparty credit risk concentration, GL-to-bank reconciliation variances, and signatory authority compliance across treasury bank accounts.
query_patterns: What is the current market value, accrued interest, and yield to maturity of each investment position held across all treasury bank accounts, grouped by instrument type and counterparty bank?
Which bank accounts have a GL-to-bank reconciliation variance above a defined tolerance as of the latest month-end, and what is the current credit rating of the corresponding counterparty banks?
What is the total counterparty exposure concentration by bank as of today, broken down by deposits, investments, and derivative MTM values, and which banks exceed the portfolio concentration limit?

14.description: This community represents the cash flow forecasting and forecast accuracy domain, containing all tables needed to manage versioned forecast runs and evaluate their predictive performance. It holds forecast snapshot metadata (forecast_snapshot), projected cash flows by entity, account, and business category (forecast_cash_flow), and a direct forecast-versus-actual variance tracking table (forecast_vs_actual) that quantifies forecast accuracy at the company, period, and flow category level. These tables support questions around forecast accuracy trends, variance attribution by category, and the evolution of cash flow projections across successive forecast model runs.
query_patterns: For the most recent monthly forecast snapshot, what is the forecast accuracy (percentage variance) by legal entity and flow category compared to the actual cash flows realised?
How has the forecasted AR collections amount for a specific entity evolved across successive forecast snapshots over the past six months, and what is the trend in forecast error over time?
Which legal entities and flow categories showed the largest absolute variance between forecast and actual in the last quarter, and were those variances predominantly positive or negative?

15.description: This community covers retail payment activity and fraud loss at the point of sale, linking individual POS transactions and membership fee collections to confirmed fraud loss incidents. It captures transactional data across all retail channels (in-warehouse, e-commerce, kiosk, mobile) and membership tiers, together with fraud loss records that detail attack vectors, authentication methods, and recovery amounts linked back to specific authorisation events. These tables support analysis of payment collection success rates, channel and membership tier revenue, and the financial impact of fraud by attack vector and sales channel.
query_patterns: What is the membership fee collection success rate by tier and sales channel for each subsidiary this month, and what is the total value of fees that resulted in a chargeback or refund?
Which point-of-sale channels and store locations have the highest confirmed fraud loss amounts in the past quarter, and what authentication methods were in use for those transactions?
What is the total revenue from POS transactions by payment method and sales channel for each month this year, and what share was subject to a confirmed fraud loss?

16.description: This community brings together corporate equity actions and payment file operations, capturing share buybacks and dividend distributions executed by the group holding entity alongside the ISO pain.001 payment files and exceptions generated to settle those and other corporate disbursements. It records equity event details (action type, share count, payout amount, program name) alongside payment file transmission status, aggregate file values, and individual exception records that identify processing failures such as OFAC holds, duplicate payments, or file format errors. These tables support questions around the operational execution of corporate equity programs, payment file throughput and error rates, and the cost and volume of payment exceptions requiring remediation.
query_patterns: What is the total payout amount and share count for each equity action (buyback, dividend) executed under each corporate program this year, and what was the associated payment file transmission status for the settlement?
How many payment exceptions were raised per exception type (BANK_VALIDATION, OFAC_HOLD, DUPLICATE, etc.) in the last quarter, and what was the average remediation cost and resolution time per type?
Which payment files submitted in the past month were acknowledged with a NACK status, and are any of those files linked to equity action settlements or high-value corporate disbursements?

glossary_terms.description: Automated Clearing House — a batch-based electronic payment network used for direct debits and credit transfers. In this context, relates to ACH returns (failed or rejected ACH transactions) tracked in the ach_return table.
A rejected or returned ACH transaction, representing a payment that could not be processed successfully. Tracked in the ach_return table with resolution status and associated bank account.

The internal code identifying a specific company bank account (e.g. GR_SE_OPERATING_1, GR_GB_OPERATING_1). Users may refer to this as 'bank account', 'account code', 'account reference', or 'company bank account'.
Indicates whether an ACH return has been actioned/closed (True = Resolved) or is still open/pending (False = Unresolved). Users may ask for 'open', 'closed', 'actioned', or 'outstanding' returns.
A merchant acquiring bank or payment processor that processes card transactions on behalf of merchants. Also referred to as processor, payment provider, or acquiring bank.
Internal system code identifying a payment acquirer (e.g. ADYEN = Adyen, STRIPE = Stripe, CHASE_PAYTECH = JPMorgan Chase Paymentech). Users typically refer to acquirers by their full names.
Payment acquirer/processor Adyen NV, stored in the database as acquirer code 'ADYEN'.
Payment acquirer/processor Stripe Payments, stored in the database as acquirer code 'STRIPE'.
Payment acquirer Elavon (a subsidiary of US Bancorp), stored in the database as acquirer code 'ELAVON'.
Payment acquirer Fiserv, formerly known as First Data, stored in the database as acquirer code 'FISERV'.
Payment acquirer JPMorgan Chase Merchant Services, stored in the database as acquirer code 'CHASE_PAYTECH'.
Payment acquirer FIS Worldpay, stored in the database as acquirer code 'FIS_WORLDPAY'.
Payment acquirer Bank of America Merchant Services, stored in the database as acquirer code 'BANK_OF_AMERICA_MS'.
Payment acquirer Global Payments Inc, stored in the database as acquirer code 'GLOBAL_PAYMENTS'.

The parent or partner bank that sponsors an acquirer's processing activity (e.g. BANK_BAC = Bank of America, BANK_JPM = JPMorgan Chase, BANK_USR = US Bancorp). Users may refer to this as 'parent bank', 'issuing bank', or 'banking partner'.
Bank of America, referenced as the sponsoring bank code 'BANK_BAC' in the acquirer table.
JPMorgan Chase, referenced as the sponsoring bank code 'BANK_JPM' in the acquirer table.
US Bancorp, referenced as the sponsoring bank code 'BANK_USR' in the acquirer table.

The bank account into which an acquirer settles merchant funds (e.g. USA_RGNL_OPERATING = US Regional Operating Account). Users may call this 'clearing account', 'funding account', or 'operating account'.
Americas region — the geographic grouping covering North and South America in the acquirer region dimension.
Europe, Middle East & Africa — the geographic region grouping used in the acquirer region dimension.
A flag indicating whether an acquirer is designated as a strategic/preferred partner (true = strategic, false = non-strategic). Users may ask for 'preferred', 'priority', or 'key' acquirers.
The date on which an acquirer was activated and went live. Users may refer to this as 'go-live date', 'activation date', 'start date', or 'contract start date'.
A bank account used for day-to-day operational cash flows, such as payroll or regional operating activity. Seen across both ACH return bank account references and acquirer settlement accounts.
A bank account designated for payroll disbursements, identified by '_PAYROLL_' in the bank account reference codes (e.g. GR_US_INC_PAYROLL_1, GR_IT_PAYROLL_1).
