A bank account used for cash concentration or pooling purposes, identified by '_CONCENTRATION' in bank account reference codes (e.g. IHB_AUD_CONCENTRATION).
In-House Bank — an internal banking structure where a corporate treasury acts as a bank for its subsidiaries. Seen in the bank account reference IHB_AUD_CONCENTRATION.
The geographic region to which an acquirer is assigned (AMER or EMEA). Users may refer to this as 'territory', 'operating region', or 'regional grouping'.
The unique system-generated identifier for an acquirer record. Users may refer to this as 'acquirer ID', 'record ID', or 'system ID'.
Service Level Agreement — a contractual commitment between a merchant and an acquirer/processor defining performance thresholds such as uptime, authorisation response time, and settlement timing.
The contractually agreed minimum system availability percentage an acquirer must maintain, stored as acquirer_contract.uptime_sla_pct.
The maximum authorisation response time in milliseconds guaranteed by the acquirer under contract, stored as acquirer_contract.auth_response_sla_ms.
The contractually committed number of business days within which an acquirer must settle funds, stored as acquirer_contract.settlement_sla_business_days.
The number of days of advance written notice required before a contract renewal date to opt out or renegotiate, stored as acquirer_contract.renewal_notice_days.

A flag indicating whether an acquirer contract automatically renews at expiry (true = Auto-renews at expiry) or requires manual action (false = Manual renewal required), stored as acquirer_contract.auto_renew.
Payment processor Chase Paymentech, referenced in the database as acquirer_ref = 'CHASE_PAYTECH'.
The percentage of payment authorisation attempts that are approved by the acquirer, stored as acquirer_sla_metric.auth_rate_pct. A key indicator of acquirer performance.
The average time in milliseconds taken by the acquirer to respond to an authorisation request, stored as acquirer_sla_metric.avg_response_time_ms.
Milliseconds — the unit used to measure authorisation response times (both SLA targets and observed averages) in this system.
Percentage — the unit used to express uptime SLA targets and authorisation approval rates in this system.
Working days (excluding weekends and public holidays) used as the unit for settlement SLA commitments in acquirer contracts.
The date on which an SLA performance metric was recorded or observed, stored as acquirer_sla_metric.measurement_date.
A contract that automatically rolls over at expiry without requiring explicit renewal action, equivalent to auto_renew = true in the database.
The unique system-generated identifier for an SLA metric record, stored as acquirer_sla_metric.uuid.
The number of times a service provider has violated the terms of its SLA within a given period. Maps to acquirer_sla_metric.sla_breach_count.
The percentage of settlements completed within the contractually agreed timeframe. Maps to acquirer_sla_metric.settlement_on_time_pct.
The percentage of time a payment or treasury platform is operational and available. Maps to acquirer_sla_metric.uptime_pct.
The total number of service incidents, outages, or issues logged against a provider in a given period. Maps to acquirer_sla_metric.incident_count.
Accounts Payable — the treasury function responsible for tracking and paying outstanding vendor invoices. Maps to the ap_invoice table.
A unique alphanumeric reference code identifying a specific AP invoice (e.g. AP-00112135). Maps to ap_invoice.invoice_number.
A third-party supplier or payee to whom the company owes payment. Users may say 'vendor', 'supplier', or 'payee'; the database stores this as vendor_ref in ap_invoice.

A registered business unit or subsidiary identified by a company code (e.g. GR_US_INC, GR_GB). Users may refer to these as 'company', 'entity', 'subsidiary', or by country name. Maps to ap_invoice.company_ref.
The Australian legal entity, stored as GR_AU in ap_invoice.company_ref.
The French legal entity, stored as GR_FR in ap_invoice.company_ref.
The Brazilian legal entity, stored as GR_BR in ap_invoice.company_ref.
The German legal entity, stored as GR_DE in ap_invoice.company_ref.
The Japanese legal entity, stored as GR_JP in ap_invoice.company_ref.
The United Kingdom legal entity, stored as GR_GB in ap_invoice.company_ref.
The Mexican legal entity, stored as GR_MX in ap_invoice.company_ref.
The Hong Kong legal entity, stored as GR_HK in ap_invoice.company_ref.
The Swedish legal entity, stored as GR_SE in ap_invoice.company_ref.
The Polish legal entity, stored as GR_PL in ap_invoice.company_ref.
The US incorporated legal entity, stored as GR_US_INC in ap_invoice.company_ref.
The Canadian legal entity, stored as GR_CA in ap_invoice.company_ref.
The Italian legal entity, stored as GR_IT in ap_invoice.company_ref.
The central treasury legal entity, stored as GR_TREASURY in ap_invoice.company_ref.
The group holdings legal entity, stored as GR_HOLDINGS in ap_invoice.company_ref.
The South Korean legal entity, stored as GR_KR in ap_invoice.company_ref.
The Spanish legal entity, stored as GR_ES in ap_invoice.company_ref.
The United Arab Emirates legal entity, stored as GR_AE in ap_invoice.company_ref.
The date on which a vendor invoice was raised or issued. Maps to ap_invoice.issue_date.
The date by which an AP invoice must be paid to avoid late payment. Maps to ap_invoice.due_date.
Days Payable Outstanding — a treasury metric measuring the average number of days a company takes to pay its vendors. Calculated from ap_invoice issue and due dates.
A vendor categorised under capital expenditure, identified by vendor codes prefixed with TP_CAPEX_ (e.g. TP_CAPEX_0001). Maps to ap_invoice.vendor_ref.
A vendor categorised under IT spend, identified by vendor codes prefixed with TP_IT_ (e.g. TP_IT_0001). Maps to ap_invoice.vendor_ref.
A vendor categorised under marketing spend, identified by vendor codes prefixed with TP_MKTG_ (e.g. TP_MKTG_0001). Maps to ap_invoice.vendor_ref.
A ratio expressed as a fraction of 100, used for SLA metrics such as uptime_pct and settlement_on_time_pct. Users may express this as %, 'percent', 'rate', or 'ratio'.
Universally Unique Identifier — the internal primary key for an AP invoice record. Maps to ap_invoice.uuid.
Days Sales Outstanding — measures the average number of days it takes to collect payment after an invoice is issued. Calculated from ar_invoice.issue_date and ar_invoice.paid_date.
Month-to-Date — filters or aggregates invoice/payment data from the first day of the current month up to today. Applied against ar_invoice.issue_date, ar_invoice.due_date, or ar_invoice.paid_date.
Year-to-Date — filters or aggregates invoice/payment data from the first day of the current calendar year up to today. Applied against date columns on ar_invoice.
Quarter-to-Date — filters or aggregates invoice/payment data from the first day of the current fiscal/calendar quarter up to today.
Accounts Receivable — the money owed to a company by its customers for invoices issued but not yet paid. Maps directly to the ar_invoice table.
A billing document issued to a customer requesting payment. Maps to the ar_invoice table. Users may refer to it by its invoice_number (e.g. AR-B2C-GR_APAC_PTE-20230503) or uuid.
The buyer or client who owes payment on an invoice. Maps to ar_invoice.customer_ref (e.g. TP_CUST_0015, RETAIL_CONSUMER).
A specific customer segment value found in ar_invoice.customer_ref as 'RETAIL_CONSUMER', representing end-consumer / B2C billing rather than a named third-party counterparty.
The date by which payment must be received, stored in ar_invoice.due_date. Overdue invoices are those where due_date has passed and paid_date is null.
The date on which payment was actually received and the invoice was settled, stored in ar_invoice.paid_date. A null value indicates the invoice is still outstanding.
An invoice where ar_invoice.due_date has passed but ar_invoice.paid_date is null — i.e. payment has not been received by the deadline.
An invoice that has not yet been paid — ar_invoice.paid_date is null regardless of whether it is overdue or still within terms.
An invoice that has been fully settled — ar_invoice.paid_date is not null.
A user account where app_user.active = true, meaning the user is currently enabled and can access the system.
A user account where app_user.active = false, meaning the account has been disabled and the user cannot access the system.
A person with access to the treasury management system. Maps to the app_user table, identified by last_name and email.
The corporate email address of a system user, stored in app_user.email (e.g. diana.patel@globalretail.com).
The family name or last name of a system user, stored in app_user.last_name (e.g. Patel, Sharma, Lopez).
An invoice paid after its due date — where ar_invoice.paid_date > ar_invoice.due_date. Used to measure collection performance and SLA breaches.
The number of days an invoice is past its due date without payment. Calculated as CURRENT_DATE minus ar_invoice.due_date where paid_date is null and due_date < today.
The number of days between invoice issuance and payment receipt. Calculated as ar_invoice.paid_date minus ar_invoice.issue_date. Feeds into DSO calculations.
Working Capital — the difference between current assets (including receivables) and current liabilities. In this system, AR invoices contribute to the receivables component of working capital.
Straight-Through Processing — automated end-to-end processing of invoices or payments without manual intervention. Relevant when assessing how many AR invoices are matched and cleared automatically.
Annual Recurring Revenue — the annualised value of recurring invoice income. Can be estimated by aggregating ar_invoice amounts over a 12-month period, particularly for repeat customers.

Business-to-Consumer — invoices raised directly to end consumers rather than corporate counterparties. Visible in ar_invoice.invoice_number prefix (e.g. AR-B2C-...) and customer_ref = RETAIL_CONSUMER.
A breakdown of outstanding AR invoices grouped by how long they have been overdue (e.g. 0–30 days, 31–60 days, 61–90 days, 90+ days). Derived from ar_invoice.due_date and ar_invoice.paid_date.

The IT Treasury Administrator role in the system, stored as the code 'IT_TREAS_ADMIN' in the actor_user column of audit_trail. Users may refer to this role as 'IT admin', 'treasury IT admin', or 'system admin'.
The head of treasury role, stored as the code 'TREAS_HEAD' in the actor_user column of audit_trail. Users may refer to this as 'treasury manager', 'head of treasury', or 'treasury lead'.
The Treasury Front Office role, stored as the code 'TREAS_FRONT' in the actor_user column of audit_trail. Users may refer to this as 'front office', 'treasury dealer', or 'trading desk'.
The Security Lead role, stored as the code 'SECURITY_LEAD' in the actor_user column of audit_trail. Users may refer to this as 'security officer', 'lead security', or 'infosec lead'.

The Global Chief Financial Officer role, stored as the code 'CFO_GLOBAL' in the actor_user column of audit_trail. Users may refer to this as 'CFO', 'chief financial officer', or 'global finance head'.
Abbreviation for Chief Financial Officer. In this system, maps to the actor_user value 'CFO_GLOBAL' (Global CFO) in the audit_trail table.

The audit_trail table that records all system changes, including who made them (actor_user), when they occurred (occurred_at), and what changed (before_image, after_image). Users may refer to this as 'change log', 'activity log', 'audit log', or 'system history'.
The user or role that performed an action, stored in the audit_trail.actor_user column. Users may refer to this as 'performed by', 'changed by', 'user', 'operator', or 'acting user'.

The state of a record before a change was applied, stored in audit_trail.before_image. Users may refer to this as 'prior state', 'old values', 'previous snapshot', 'pre-change data', or 'original record'.

The state of a record after a change was applied, stored in audit_trail.after_image. Users may refer to this as 'new state', 'updated values', 'post-change data', 'new snapshot', or 'resulting record'.
A logical grouping of bank accounts, represented in the bank_account_group table. Users may refer to this as 'account group', 'bank group', 'account pool', or 'account cluster'.

The short reference code identifying a bank account group, stored in bank_account_group.code and referenced as bank_account_group_member.account_group_code. Users may refer to this as 'group code', 'short code', 'reference code', or 'bank group code'.
An association between a bank account and a bank account group, stored in the bank_account_group_member table. Users may refer to this as 'group member', 'account in group', or 'grouped account'.

A person or role authorised to sign on behalf of a bank account, stored in the bank_account_signatory table. Users may refer to this as 'signatory', 'authorised signer', 'account signer', or 'signing authority'.
The date and time an audit event occurred, stored in audit_trail.occurred_at. Users may refer to this as 'event time', 'action timestamp', 'change date', 'audit datetime', or 'occurred on'.
A calendar defining which days are non-working/holidays for a bank branch, used to determine valid settlement and processing days. Maps to bank_branch.calendar_ref = 'STANDARD'.
The standard business day calendar code stored in bank_branch.calendar_ref. Users may refer to this as the default or standard holiday calendar.
Indicates whether a bank branch is involved in intercompany (intra-group) transactions. A True value denotes an internal/in-house bank branch used for intra-group flows.
A bank branch acting as a pass-through or correspondent in a payment chain. Maps to bank_branch.intermediary flag = True. Users may say 'correspondent bank' or 'pass-through bank'.
The main or lead branch for a given country, indicated by bank_branch.main_country_branch = True. Users may refer to this as the 'head branch' or 'country lead branch'.
A bank branch that is not the designated primary branch for its country, indicated by bank_branch.main_country_branch = False.
A code identifying the messaging responder entity for a bank branch, used in interbank communication protocols. Often associated with SWIFT messaging. Maps to bank_branch.responder_code.

The SWIFT-network identifier for the responding entity at a bank branch, synonymous with bank_branch.responder_code. SWIFT (Society for Worldwide Interbank Financial Telecommunication) codes are standard interbank messaging identifiers.
An identifier linking a bank branch to a connected treasury or banking application/system. Maps to bank_branch.id_of_application.
The type of banking service or product offered by or associated with a bank branch. Maps to bank_branch.service_name.

The communication or messaging service used for interbank interactions at a branch level. Maps to bank_branch.interact_service_name. May refer to protocols like SWIFT, FedWire, or other interbank messaging networks.
A free-text internal comment or remark attached to a bank branch record. Maps to bank_branch.memo.
The physical or postal address of a bank branch. Maps to bank_branch.address.

A treasury concept where an internal entity acts as a bank for group subsidiaries. In this schema, branches with intercompany = True are typically in-house bank branches handling intra-group payments and liquidity.
A bank that acts on behalf of another bank to process transactions, especially cross-border payments. Maps to bank_branch.intermediary = True in this schema.

Bank Identifier Code — an internationally recognised code (also called SWIFT code) used to identify banks and their branches in financial transactions. Related to bank_branch.responder_code in SWIFT messaging contexts.
Asia-Pacific — a geographic region grouping used in bank_branch.region to classify branches operating across Asian and Pacific-rim countries such as JP, KR, HK, AU, SG.
Middle East & North Africa — a geographic region grouping used in bank_branch.region, covering countries such as AE (UAE) within that corridor.
Latin America — a geographic region grouping used in bank_branch.region to classify branches in Latin American countries such as MX and BR.
Common name for the banking institution stored as BANK_BNP in bank_fee.bank_ref. Users may refer to this bank by its full or short name rather than the database code.
Common name for the banking institution stored as BANK_HSBC in bank_fee.bank_ref.
Common name for the banking institution stored as BANK_DB in bank_fee.bank_ref.
Common name for the banking institution stored as BANK_BBVA_MX in bank_fee.bank_ref, representing BBVA's Mexican entity.
Mitsubishi UFJ Financial Group — the banking institution stored as BANK_MUFG in bank_fee.bank_ref.
Common name for the banking institution stored as BANK_CITI in bank_fee.bank_ref.
Australia and New Zealand Banking Group — the banking institution stored as BANK_ANZ in bank_fee.bank_ref.
Nordic financial services institution stored as BANK_NORDEA in bank_fee.bank_ref.
Common name for the banking institution stored as BANK_RBC in bank_fee.bank_ref.
Common name for the banking institution stored as BANK_SCB in bank_fee.bank_ref.
Refers to the regional US banking institution stored as BANK_USR in bank_fee.bank_ref.
Users commonly refer to 'bank', 'lender', or 'counterparty' when querying banking institutions. In the database, this maps to bank_fee.bank_ref or bank_branch records.
A bank branch record stored in the bank_branch table. Users may say 'office', 'location', or 'entity' when referring to a branch.
A charge levied by a bank for a service, stored in the bank_fee table. Users may refer to these as charges, billing items, or service fees.
A bank account referenced by bank_fee.bank_account_ref. Users may say 'account', 'account code', 'account key', or 'account label' to refer to the bank account identifier.
A type of bank account used for day-to-day operational transactions, identified by '_OPERATING_' in bank_fee.bank_account_ref values (e.g. GR_GB_OPERATING_1, GR_US_INC_OPERATING_1).
A type of bank account used for collecting receipts, identified by '_COLLECTION_' in bank_fee.bank_account_ref values (e.g. GR_GB_COLLECTION_1, GR_JP_COLLECTION_1).

A regional-level operating account, identified by the '_RGNL_OPERATING' suffix in bank_fee.bank_account_ref values (e.g. EUR_RGNL_OPERATING, USA_RGNL_OPERATING, APC_RGNL_OPERATING, LAT_RGNL_OPERATING).

A numeric code in bank_fee.service_code that categorises the type of banking service being billed. Users may refer to this as 'fee type', 'charge code', or 'billing service category'. Known values: 100, 251, 260, 270, 271, 300.
The month-end date in bank_fee.statement_period representing the billing or invoice period for a bank fee. Users may call this 'billing period', 'billing month', 'fee period', or 'invoice period'.
ISO 2-letter country code stored in bank_branch.country_code (e.g. US, GB, AE, SG). Users may simply say 'country' or 'country of operation' when filtering by geography.
Geographic grouping stored in bank_branch.region (EMEA, APAC, AMER, MENA, LATAM). Users may say 'business region', 'operating region', or 'regional grouping'.
Free-text contact information for a bank branch stored in bank_branch.contact. Users may refer to this as 'branch contact', 'contact information', or 'branch contacts'.
The unique identifier (UUID) for a bank fee record stored in bank_fee.uuid. Users may call this 'record ID', 'bank fee identifier', or 'unique key'.
The date on which a bank fee was applied or billed. Maps to bank_fee.charge_date in the database.
The number of transactions or service instances associated with a bank fee line item. Maps to bank_fee.units.
The actual fee amount billed by the bank for a given service or transaction. Maps to bank_fee.charged_amount.
The anticipated or contracted fee amount based on the agreed rate card, used as a benchmark against the charged amount. Maps to bank_fee.expected_amount.
The difference between the charged amount and the expected amount, representing overbilling or excess charges by the bank. Maps to bank_fee.overage_amount.
The ISO currency code in which the bank fee is denominated. Currently USD (US Dollar) in the database. Maps to bank_fee.currency_code.
US Dollar — the currency code used for bank fee transactions. Alias: 'US Dollar'. Maps to bank_fee.currency_code = 'USD'.
A unique identifier linking a bank fee to a specific cash flow or payment transaction. Maps to bank_fee.cash_flow_ref.
A unique identifier pointing to the pricing agreement or fee schedule used to calculate the expected fee. Maps to bank_fee.rate_card_ref.
Indicates whether a bank fee record has been marked for review, exception handling, or dispute. True = Flagged for review; False = Not flagged. Maps to bank_fee.flagged.
A unique identifier for a bank group record. Maps to bank_group.uuid.
The difference between the actual charged amount and the expected (contracted) amount for a bank fee, used to identify overbilling or pricing discrepancies. Derived from bank_fee.overage_amount.
A contractual pricing schedule agreed between the company and the bank that defines expected fees per service or transaction type. Referenced via bank_fee.rate_card_ref.
A charge levied by a bank for treasury or cash management services such as wire transfers, account maintenance, or ACH processing. Corresponds to the bank_fee table.
A wire transfer — an electronic funds transfer typically used for large, same-day domestic or international payments. Often associated with higher bank fees.
A unit of measure equal to one-hundredth of a percentage point (0.01%), commonly used to express fee rates, interest rates, and variances in treasury contexts.
Foreign Exchange — relates to currency conversion fees that may appear in bank fee data. Currently all fees are denominated in USD, but FX fees may still be charged on cross-currency transactions.
Unique identifier for a brain evaluation record. Users may refer to this as evaluation ID, record ID, or unique ID, which maps to brain_evaluation.uuid in the database.
Identifier for the user who submitted or triggered an evaluation. Users may say user ID, requestor ID, or submitter code, which maps to brain_evaluation.user_code in the database.
The natural-language question or prompt submitted by a user for evaluation. Maps to brain_evaluation.query_text. Users may call this the question, prompt, input query, or search query.
The date and time at which an evaluation was run or processed. Maps to brain_evaluation.evaluated_at. Users may refer to this as evaluation time, run timestamp, or execution time.

The set of facts or knowledge snippets that were actively used during an evaluation's reasoning process. Maps to brain_evaluation.facts_applied. Also called used facts, knowledge applied, or reasoning facts.
The paths or connections traversed through the knowledge graph during reasoning. Maps to brain_evaluation.edges_traversed. Users may call these traversed paths, reasoning paths, or path steps.

Detected contradictions or inconsistencies identified during an evaluation, such as conflicting rules or data points. Maps to brain_evaluation.flagged_conflicts. Also referred to as detected conflicts, rule conflicts, or inconsistencies.

The final output or conclusion generated by an evaluation, summarising the response to the user's query. Maps to brain_evaluation.answer_summary. Users may call this the response summary, evaluation result, or output summary.

The initial or foundational facts provided as input to seed the reasoning process of an evaluation. Maps to brain_evaluation.seed_facts. Also called starting facts, base facts, root facts, or input facts.

Numerical scores indicating the relevance or confidence of retrieved facts used in an evaluation. Maps to brain_evaluation.retrieval_scores. Users may call these relevance scores, confidence scores, fact scores, or match scores.
Budget code representing the Operations budget. Users may refer to this as 'ops budget', 'operating budget', or 'operational spend'.
Budget code representing the Capital Expenditure budget. Users may refer to this as 'capex budget', 'capital budget', or 'investment budget'.
Budget code representing the Tax & Duties budget. Users may refer to this as 'tax budget', 'duties budget', or 'tax provision'.
Budget code representing the Treasury & Financing budget. Users may refer to this as 'treasury budget', 'financing budget', or 'treas budget'.
Company reference code for the Group Holdings legal entity. Users may refer to this as 'group', 'holdco', 'parent entity', or 'group holdings'.
Company reference code for the US Incorporated entity. Users may refer to this as 'US entity', 'US inc', 'American subsidiary', or 'US subsidiary'.
Company reference code for the European BV legal entity. Users may refer to this as 'EU entity', 'European entity', 'BV', 'European subsidiary', or 'EU BV'.
Capital Expenditure allocation bucket. Represents capital deployed toward long-term asset investment. Users may say 'capex spend', 'capital investment', or 'fixed asset spend'.
Mergers & Acquisitions allocation bucket. Represents capital deployed toward M&A activity. Users may say 'M&A', 'mergers', 'acquisitions', or 'deal spend'.
Dividend Distributions allocation bucket. Represents capital deployed as dividend payments to shareholders. Users may say 'divs', 'dividend payments', or 'shareholder distributions'.
Debt Repayment allocation bucket. Represents capital deployed to reduce outstanding debt. Users may say 'debt repayment', 'debt reduction', 'loan paydown', or 'deleveraging'.
Share Buybacks allocation bucket. Represents capital deployed to repurchase company shares. Users may say 'share repurchase', 'stock buyback', 'buyback programme', or 'repurchase'.
Currency code for British Pound Sterling. Users may refer to this as 'pounds', 'sterling', 'pound sterling', 'GBP', or '£'.
Currency code for the Euro. Users may refer to this as 'euros', 'euro', '€', or 'EUR'.

The reporting period end date for capital allocation records. Users may refer to this as 'reporting date', 'quarter end', 'as-of date', 'financial period', or 'period end'. Values align to quarter-end dates (e.g. 2024-03-31).

The actual amount of capital allocated and disbursed for a given bucket, entity, and period. Maps to capital_allocation_actual.amount. Users may say 'actual spend', 'disbursement', 'capital outflow', or 'allocation amount'.
The type or purpose of a capital allocation, stored as the 'bucket' field. Users may say 'use of capital', 'capital use type', 'spend category', or 'deployment bucket'.

A classification code that categorises financial activity into budget segments such as operations, capex, tax, or treasury. Maps to budget_code.code. Users may say 'cost code', 'GL code', 'budget category code', or 'budget classification'.
General Ledger code. Used interchangeably with budget code by non-technical users to identify a budget category or cost centre. Maps to budget_code.code.

A measure in the brain evaluation context representing the number of hops or steps taken during graph traversal or reasoning expansion. Users may say 'hop count', 'traversal depth', 'graph hops', 'expansion depth', or 'reasoning steps'.
Unique identifier for a card authorization record in the database (UUID format). Used to look up or reference a specific authorization event.
Point-of-sale transaction reference identifier assigned by the terminal or merchant system, used to correlate a card authorization back to the originating POS transaction.
The payment card scheme or brand that routes and governs card authorization transactions (e.g. Visa, Mastercard). Stored in the database as network_code.
Card network represented by the database code VISA. Users may refer to it as 'Visa' or 'VI'.
Card network represented by the database code MASTERCARD. Users may refer to it as 'Mastercard', 'MC', or 'Master Card'.
Card network represented by the database code AMEX. Users may refer to it as 'American Express', 'Amex', or 'AX'.
Card network represented by the database code DISCOVER.
Proprietary/closed-loop card network represented by the database code COSTCO_PRIVATE. Used for Costco-branded private label cards.
Card network represented by the database code UNIONPAY. Chinese payment card scheme commonly used for cross-border transactions.
Card network represented by the database code INTERAC. Canadian debit card network.
Card network represented by the database code JCB. Japanese card scheme (Japan Credit Bureau).
Bank Identification Number — the first 6 digits of a payment card number that identify the issuing institution, card brand, and card type. Also known as the Issuer Identification Number (IIN).
The date and time at which a card authorization request was sent to the payment network or processor.
The date and time at which a card authorization response was received back from the payment network or processor.
The elapsed time in milliseconds between sending an authorization request and receiving a response. A key SLA metric for payment processing performance.
The outcome of a card authorization request. Database stores codes: APPROVED, DECLINED, TIMEOUT, ERROR.
Authorization decision code APPROVED — the transaction was authorized successfully by the issuer.
Authorization decision code DECLINED — the transaction was refused by the issuer or processor.
Authorization decision code TIMEOUT — no response was received from the network within the allowed window, resulting in a no-response / timeout outcome.
Authorization decision code ERROR — a technical or system error prevented the authorization from completing successfully.
The percentage of card authorization requests that result in an APPROVED decision. Calculated as approved authorizations divided by total authorizations.
The percentage of card authorization requests that result in a DECLINED decision. A key metric for fraud monitoring and payment optimization.
The policy-defined or framework-mandated target weight for a capital allocation category, expressed as a percentage. Stored as a decimal (e.g. 0.20 = 20%).
The long-term, policy-driven target weighting of capital across asset classes or investment categories, as defined in the treasury investment framework.
The distribution of treasury capital across various asset classes, instruments, or business units, measured both as actual holdings and framework-defined targets.

A numeric code returned by the card issuer indicating why an authorization request was declined. Maps to card_authorization.decline_reason_code. Common values: 05 (Do Not Honor), 14 (Invalid Card Number), 51 (Insufficient Funds), 54 (Expired Card), 57 (Transaction Not Permitted to Cardholder).
Decline reason code 05. A generic issuer decline indicating the card-issuing bank has refused the transaction without a specific reason.
Decline reason code 14. Indicates the card number submitted in the authorization request does not exist or is incorrectly formatted.
Decline reason code 51. Indicates the cardholder does not have enough available credit or balance to cover the transaction amount.
Decline reason code 54. Indicates the card being used has passed its expiration date.
Decline reason code 57. Indicates the transaction type is not allowed for this cardholder or card product.
The monetary value submitted for approval in a card authorization request. Maps to card_authorization.amount.
A three-letter ISO 4217 standard code representing the transaction currency. Maps to card_authorization.currency_code. Supported values: USD, EUR, GBP, JPY, CAD, AUD, KRW, HKD.
ISO 4217 code for the Japanese Yen. Used as a currency_code value in card_authorization transactions.
ISO 4217 code for the Canadian Dollar. Used as a currency_code value in card_authorization transactions.
ISO 4217 code for the Australian Dollar. Used as a currency_code value in card_authorization transactions.
ISO 4217 code for the South Korean Won. Used as a currency_code value in card_authorization transactions.
ISO 4217 code for the Hong Kong Dollar. Used as a currency_code value in card_authorization transactions.

A bucketed dimension grouping authorization transactions by spend value. Maps to card_authorization.transaction_size_band. Bands: LT_25 (<$25), 25_100 ($25–$100), 100_500 ($100–$500), 500_5000 ($500–$5,000), GT_5000 (>$5,000).
Transaction size band for authorizations with an amount less than $25. Maps to card_authorization.transaction_size_band = 'LT_25'.
Transaction size band for authorizations between $25 and $100. Maps to card_authorization.transaction_size_band = '25_100'.
Transaction size band for authorizations between $100 and $500. Maps to card_authorization.transaction_size_band = '100_500'.
Transaction size band for authorizations between $500 and $5,000. Maps to card_authorization.transaction_size_band = '500_5000'.
Transaction size band for authorizations greater than $5,000. Maps to card_authorization.transaction_size_band = 'GT_5000'.
Geographic or business operating region associated with a card authorization. Maps to card_authorization.region. Values: AMER, EMEA, APAC, LATAM.
The outcome of the 3D Secure (3DS) strong customer authentication flow for a card authorization. Maps to card_authorization.auth_3ds_status. Values: NOT_ATTEMPTED, FRICTIONLESS, CHALLENGED, FAILED.
Strong Customer Authentication — a regulatory requirement (e.g., under PSD2) mandating multi-factor authentication for electronic payments. Reflected in card_authorization.auth_3ds_status.
3DS status indicating that 3D Secure authentication was not initiated for the transaction. Maps to card_authorization.auth_3ds_status = 'NOT_ATTEMPTED'.

3DS status indicating the transaction passed 3D Secure authentication without requiring direct cardholder interaction (no challenge presented). Maps to card_authorization.auth_3ds_status = 'FRICTIONLESS'.
3DS status indicating the cardholder was presented with an authentication challenge (e.g., OTP or biometric) during the transaction. Maps to card_authorization.auth_3ds_status = 'CHALLENGED'.
3DS status indicating the 3D Secure authentication attempt was unsuccessful. Maps to card_authorization.auth_3ds_status = 'FAILED'.
A unique identifier representing the device or browser used to initiate a card transaction, used for fraud detection and risk scoring. Maps to card_authorization.device_fingerprint.
Card Not Present — a transaction type where the physical card is not used at a terminal, typically e-commerce or phone orders. Maps to card_authorization.cnp_indicator = true.
Indicates the physical card was present at the point of sale during the transaction. Maps to card_authorization.cnp_indicator = false.
A contiguous range of BIN values assigned to a card program or issuer, defined by a lower and upper bound. Corresponds to the card_bin_range table with fields bin_low (and implicitly bin_high).
A short alphanumeric reference identifying a legal entity enrolled in a card rebate program. Maps to the company_ref column in card_rebate_program.
User-facing name for the GR_HOLDINGS database code, representing the Group Holdings legal entity in the card rebate program.
User-facing name for the GR_US_INC database code, representing the US Incorporated legal entity in the card rebate program.
User-facing name for the GR_EU_BV database code, representing the European BV legal entity in the card rebate program.
Abbreviation for Purchasing Card. Maps to the PURCHASING_CARD value in the program_type dimension of card_rebate_program. Used for corporate procurement card programs.
A card program type representing single-use or tokenised virtual payment cards. Maps to VIRTUAL_CARD in the program_type dimension of card_rebate_program.
A card program type representing general commercial/corporate card programs. Maps to COMMERCIAL_CARD in the program_type dimension of card_rebate_program.
The minimum qualifying spend amount required to reach a rebate tier. Maps to rebate_tier_threshold in card_rebate_program.
Basis Points — a unit equal to 1/100th of 1% (0.01%), used to express rebate rates in card programs. Maps to rebate_bps_at_target in card_rebate_program.
The date from which a card rebate program becomes active. Maps to effective_from in card_rebate_program.
The date on which a card rebate program ends or is no longer valid. Maps to effective_to in card_rebate_program.
A unique identifier for a card settlement batch record. Maps to the uuid column in card_settlement_batch.
Common abbreviation for American Express. Maps to the AMEX network code in card_settlement_batch.
The currency in which a card settlement batch is funded or remitted to the merchant. Maps to settlement_currency in card_settlement_batch.
The percentage or basis-point rate of spend that is returned to the company as a rebate when the target spend tier is reached. Maps to rebate_bps_at_target in card_rebate_program.

A commercial agreement between a company and a card issuer/network that returns a percentage of card spend to the company once defined spend thresholds are met. Represented by the card_rebate_program table.
A grouped record of card transactions submitted by an acquirer for settlement and funding. Represented by the card_settlement_batch table.
The timestamp at which a card settlement batch was closed and submitted for processing. Maps to card_settlement_batch.batch_close_ts.
The timestamp at which the payment processor confirmed settlement of a card batch. Maps to card_settlement_batch.processor_settle_ts.
The timestamp at which funds from a settled card batch were credited to the bank account. Maps to card_settlement_batch.bank_deposit_ts.
The US-based regional operating bank account used for card settlement deposits. Stored in the database as the code USA_RGNL_OPERATING in card_settlement_batch.bank_account_ref.
The Euro-region operating bank account used for card settlement deposits. Stored in the database as the code EUR_RGNL_OPERATING in card_settlement_batch.bank_account_ref.
The fourth US incorporated entity operating bank account used for card settlement deposits. Stored in the database as the code GR_US_INC_OP_4 in card_settlement_batch.bank_account_ref.
A reference code identifying which bank account received settlement funds for a card batch. Maps to card_settlement_batch.bank_account_ref.
The total gross card sales volume processed in a settlement batch before any deductions. Maps to card_settlement_batch.gross_sales_amount.
The total value of refunds, returns, or reversals processed within a settlement batch. Maps to card_settlement_batch.refund_amount.
The total value of chargebacks or disputed transactions deducted within a settlement batch. Maps to card_settlement_batch.chargeback_amount.
Fees paid to card-issuing banks as a cost of accepting card payments, deducted during settlement. Maps to card_settlement_batch.interchange_amount.
Fees charged by card networks/schemes (e.g. Visa, Mastercard) assessed on transaction volume, deducted during settlement. Maps to card_settlement_batch.network_assessment_amount.
The fee or markup retained by the payment processor/acquirer for processing card transactions, deducted during settlement. Maps to card_settlement_batch.processor_margin_amount.

The net funds deposited to the bank after subtracting refunds, chargebacks, interchange fees, network assessment fees, and processor margin from gross sales. Derived as: gross_sales_amount - refund_amount - chargeback_amount - interchange_amount - network_assessment_amount - processor_margin_amount.
The elapsed time between batch close and bank deposit, indicating how long it takes for card sales to convert to available funds. Derived from bank_deposit_ts minus batch_close_ts.
A unit multiplier (1,000,000) used by business users when expressing large dollar amounts for gross sales, refunds, chargebacks, and fees (e.g. '$5M in gross sales').
A unit multiplier (1,000,000,000) used by business users when expressing very large dollar amounts for gross sales volume across settlement batches (e.g. '$1B processed').
The card network or scheme (e.g. Visa, Mastercard, Amex, Discover) that assesses network fees on settlement batches. Relates to network_assessment_amount.

The period during which card settlement funds are in transit between batch close and bank deposit, representing temporary unavailability of cash. Measured by the gap between batch_close_ts and bank_deposit_ts.
Ancillary or miscellaneous charges deducted within a card settlement batch that do not fall under standard interchange fees.
The total number of individual payment transactions included within a single card settlement batch.
The total face value of a card transaction before any fees or deductions are applied; the pre-fee transaction amount on a settlement line.
The absolute dollar value of the interchange fee charged by the card issuer/network on a given settlement line transaction.
A unique identifier assigned to a card settlement batch, used to link individual settlement lines back to their parent batch record.
A unique identifier for an individual card authorization event, used to trace a settlement line back to the originating payment approval.
The unique identifier for a single record within the card settlement line table, distinguishing each individual transaction entry.
A flag value indicating that a card settlement batch was processed within the contracted Service Level Agreement timeframe (True = on time; False = late/breached).
A flag value indicating that a card settlement batch failed to be processed within the contracted Service Level Agreement timeframe (False = late/breached).
The per-transaction fee rate charged by the card issuer or network, expressed in basis points (bps), representing the cost of card acceptance on each settlement line.
A grouped collection of card payment transactions submitted together for settlement processing, carrying aggregate metrics such as net settlement amount, transaction count, and fee totals.
An individual transaction-level record within a card settlement batch, detailing the gross amount, interchange fee, and authorization reference for a single payment.

The fee charged by the card scheme/network (e.g. Visa, Mastercard) per transaction, stored in network_assessment_amount. Represents the cost levied by the card network on the acquirer/merchant.
Miscellaneous or ancillary fees associated with a card settlement line that do not fall under network assessment or processor margin, stored in other_fees_amount.

The country of the bank that issued the payment card used in the transaction, stored as an ISO country code in issuer_country. Common values include US (United States), CN (China), DE (Germany), GB (United Kingdom), FR (France), JP (Japan), CA (Canada), AU (Australia), MX (Mexico).
Plain-language name for the issuer country code 'US' in the issuer_country column.
Plain-language name for the issuer country code 'CN' in the issuer_country column.
Plain-language name for the issuer country code 'DE' in the issuer_country column.

A card transaction where the issuing bank's country differs from the merchant's country. Stored as a boolean flag in cross_border; true = international/cross-border, false = domestic.
A card transaction where the issuing bank's country matches the merchant's country. Represented by cross_border = false in the database.
A unique identifier for a treasury or bank account in the cash_balance table, stored in account_ref. Examples include GR_DE_OPERATING_1, IHB_GBP_DISBURSEMENT, EUR_RGNL_OPERATING.

A treasury account used to make outbound payments such as payroll, vendor payments, or intercompany transfers. Identified by '_DISBURSEMENT' in account_ref values such as IHB_GBP_DISBURSEMENT, IHB_EUR_DISBURSEMENT.
A dedicated bank account used for tax-related payments and obligations. Identified by '_TAX' in account_ref values such as GR_MX_TAX_1, GR_ES_TAX_1, GR_BR_TAX_1, GR_IE_TAX_1.

A bank account designated to receive inbound payments or collections from customers. Identified by '_COLLECTION' in account_ref values such as GR_IE_COLLECTION_1, GR_JP_COLLECTION_1, GR_GB_COLLECTION_1.

A treasury account that serves a regional group of entities rather than a single country. Identified by 'RGNL' in account_ref values such as EUR_RGNL_OPERATING, LAT_RGNL_OPERATING, LAT_RGNL_CONCENTRATION.
The date as of which a cash balance is recorded in the cash_balance table. Used to filter or aggregate balances at a point in time.

Prefix used in account_ref codes to denote a specific legal entity group or geographic region (e.g. GR_DE_OPERATING_1, GR_MX_PAYROLL_1). Likely refers to a subsidiary group or group-regional entity tier.
Prefix used in account_ref codes to denote Latin America regional accounts (e.g. LAT_RGNL_OPERATING, LAT_RGNL_CONCENTRATION).

The weighted average effective rate across multiple transactions or fee components (e.g. blended FX rate, blended card fee rate). Derived by dividing total fees or converted amounts by total transaction volume.
The settlement or clearing date on which a transaction is considered effective for cash balance purposes. Maps to VALUE_DATE in cash_balance.date_basis.
The accounting date on which a transaction is recorded or booked. Maps to TRANSACTION_DATE in cash_balance.date_basis.
The date convention used to compute a cash balance — either Transaction Date or Value Date. Maps to cash_balance.date_basis.
A cash balance that includes posted/booked transactions that have already occurred. Controlled by the cash_balance.includes_actual flag.
A cash balance that includes same-day or real-time transactions not yet end-of-day settled. Controlled by cash_balance.includes_intraday.
A cash balance that includes transactions confirmed by the bank. Maps to CONFIRMED in cash_balance.cash_flow_status and cash_balance.includes_confirmed flag.
A cash balance that includes forecasted or projected transactions not yet confirmed by the bank. Maps to ESTIMATED in cash_balance.cash_flow_status and cash_balance.includes_estimated flag.
The monetary amount held in a bank account at a given point in time, subject to date basis and transaction inclusion filters. Maps to cash_balance.amount.
The ISO 4217 currency code in which a cash balance or cash flow is denominated. Maps to cash_balance.currency_code.

ISO 4217 code for the Swedish Krona. Used in cash_balance.currency_code.
ISO 4217 code for the Singapore Dollar. Used in cash_balance.currency_code.
ISO 4217 code for the Polish Zloty. Used in cash_balance.currency_code.
ISO 4217 code for the Swiss Franc. Used in cash_balance.currency_code.
ISO 4217 code for the UAE Dirham. Used in cash_balance.currency_code.
ISO 4217 code for the Chilean Peso. Used in cash_balance.currency_code.
A headquarter-level account used to invest surplus cash. Maps to HQ_INV_EUR and HQ_INV_USD in cash_flow.account_ref.
Headquarters — refers to the central/group treasury entity. Used as a prefix in account_ref codes HQ_INV_EUR and HQ_INV_USD.

The confirmation status of a cash flow or balance, indicating whether it has been confirmed by the bank or is still estimated/forecast. Maps to cash_balance.cash_flow_status.

0.description: Returns the sum of all cash balances across every bank account as of the prior business day.

aggregate_total: sum all account balances into a single grand total

cte_steps: filter_account_and_period: narrow balance records to the JPMorgan operating account and the last 7 calendar days
order_by_date: present daily closing balances in chronological order
required_aggregations: closing balance per day for the specified account

2.description: Lists all wire transfer payment records exceeding one million dollars that were processed today.
cte_steps: filter_wire_transfers_today: isolate payment transactions that are wire transfers, processed today, and exceed one million in amount
present_results: return the filtered list with relevant transaction details

cte_steps: filter_negative_balances_this_week: isolate balance records from the current week where the balance value is below zero
deduplicate_accounts: return a distinct list of accounts that appeared with a negative balance
required_aggregations: count or list of accounts with negative balances

balance date falls within the current week

aggregate_total: sum all qualifying ACH receipt amounts into a single total
required_aggregations: total ACH receipt amount for yesterday

5.description: Lists all bank accounts organized into groups by the currency each account is denominated in.
cte_steps: filter: narrow down records to the relevant scope
aggregate: compute the required business metrics

cte_steps: filter: narrow down records to the relevant scope
aggregate: compute the required business metrics
required_aggregations: count of open bank accounts in Canada

7.description: Returns a full daily cash position snapshot — including opening balances, inflows, outflows, and closing balances by entity and account — for last Friday.
cte_steps: filter_date: narrow all relevant records to last Friday's date
get_opening_balances: retrieve the opening balance for each account as of last Friday
aggregate_transactions: sum all inflows and outflows by account for last Friday
compute_closing_balances: combine opening balances with net transaction activity to derive closing balances
assemble_report: join account and entity reference details to produce the full daily cash position report

8.description: Returns the most recent USD-to-CAD foreign exchange rate stored in the system.
cte_steps: filter: narrow down records to the relevant scope
aggregate: compute the required business metrics
required_filters: most recent or current rate date

9.description: Compares actual cash inflows against forecasted inflows for each legal entity over the past 30 days, computing the variance percentage and flagging any entity-day combinations where the variance exceeds 10%.
cte_steps: filter_period: narrow all records to the past 30 days
aggregate_actuals: sum actual cash inflows by entity and day for the period
aggregate_forecasts: sum forecasted cash inflows by entity and day for the same period
join_actuals_and_forecasts: combine actual and forecast totals by matching entity and date
compute_variances: calculate the absolute and percentage difference between actual and forecasted inflows for each entity-day pair
flag_breaches: mark rows where the variance percentage exceeds the 10% threshold
present_results: order and present the final comparison with variance highlights by entity and date
required_aggregations: total actual inflows per entity per day
total forecasted inflows per entity per day
variance amount per entity per day
variance percentage per entity per day
required_filters: transaction or forecast date within the last 30 days
